_tags: @why("The kernel is the foundation. It handles identity, P2P transport, and consensus. Nothing else runs without it.")
P2P_KERNEL.description: Layer 0 — P2P networking core: libp2p, GossipSub, ledger sync, governance, health monitoring, security, reputation, emission.

_tags: @why("Every agent is the same code — a persistent Claude Code session with a role template and a parent. The only difference is the template.")
AGENT_SYSTEM.description: Layer 1 — Universal agent primitive: spawn, message, report, bridge queues, AI backend selection, workspace management.

_tags: @why("Stateless compute proxy pattern. Nodes decrypt for processing, then discard. Source of truth is MongoDB/S3.")
STORAGE_LAYER.description: Layer 1 — Data persistence: MongoDB direct, P2P proxy, thread storage. Nodes are stateless — user data lives on internet infrastructure.

_tags: @why("User nodes never touch credentials directly. All credential ops route through trusted compute peers via P2P.")
CREDENTIAL_SYSTEM.description: Layer 1 — Two-tier credential management: EC2 nodes have master key + MongoDB, user nodes proxy via P2P.

DEPLOY_SYSTEM.description: Layer 1-2 — App deployment: Tier 1 (S3 static), Tier 2 (EC2 PM2+nginx), backup/build/commit/rollback, upgrade protocol.

_tags: @why("Lux is a work receipt. No burning, no halving. Hard cap 10B. 0.1% relay fee. Witness-based emission.")
ECONOMY.description: Core economics: Lux ledger, accounts, transactions, emission, payment gate, contribution tracking, revenue engine.

PLATFORM_LAYER.description: Layer 2 — Platform services: scheduler, task management, project registry, file registry, genome agent, user accounts.

_tags: @why("Nodes contribute resources (AI keys, storage, compute). ResourceRouter finds the best peer for each task.")
RESOURCE_NETWORK.description: Layer 2 — Resource discovery and routing: capability detection, P2P capability registry, resource marketplace, smart routing, health monitoring.

GOVERNANCE.description: Distributed governance: proposals, votes, decisions, council, reputation-weighted voting, Sybil resistance.

CONTENT_LAYER.description: Layer 2 — Content management: SQLite content records, GossipSub sync, full-text search, content publishing, safety review.

QA_SYSTEM.description: Quality assurance: QA runner, regression suite, 14 built-in tests, three-ring QA model.

_tags: @why("All routes prefixed /v1/ since v2.2. POST /auth routes are unauthenticated. All others require Bearer token.")
API_LAYER.description: HTTP API: Fastify server, per-IP rate limiting, Bearer token auth, kernel/core/platform route modules, middleware.

NODE_CORE.description: Node entry points: PandoNode main class, CLI, TUI, config, logger. Wires all subsystems together.

SHARED_LAYER.description: Shared types, crypto utilities, and constants used by all packages.

MCP_LAYER.description: Pando MCP server for Claude Code integration: 6 tools (status, peers, balance, transfer, search, wallet).

GATEWAY.description: Web UI: Next.js 16 + Tailwind. 9 pages: Home, Chat, Scheduler, Monitor, Wallet, Network, Search, Governance, Content.

_steps.what: Any system component creates a bridge item: user_request (User via API), task_completed/task_failed (Scheduler), worker_message (Worker mid-task), health_alert (HealthMonitor), governance_decision (Governance).
bridge.enqueue(managerId, { type, source, payload, priority }). Item enters per-project FIFO queue with priority tier.
If Manager is idle: spawn immediately with this item. If Manager is busy: item waits in queue (FIFO within priority tier).

Manager receives ONE item as event prompt. Follows todo list. For user_request: assess, design workflow, create task, approve, report. For task_completed: read output, review, apply, build, commit, docs, report. For worker_message: read, respond (provide files or relay to user).
Manager process exits. bridge.setManagerIdle(managerId). If queue has more items: spawn again. If empty: do nothing. Zero cost.

AgentCommunication.summary: How all agents communicate through the Bridge Queue. THE communication model for the entire system. Every event, request, and message flows through the bridge. One item at a time. Zero cost when idle.

_steps.what: Worker posts via POST /tasks/:id/messages with type: progress, help_request, clarification, or blocked. Each message routes to bridge queue of task manager.

_tags: @gotcha("Worker CLAUDE.md tells it to check manager-response.md periodically.")
_steps.what: Manager picks up worker_message item. Reads message, finds requested files, copies to worker workspace at manager-response.md, or posts response. If user input needed: relays to user via Communication Agent.
Manager exits after responding. If worker has urgent blocking question: urgency=direct bypasses Manager queue, sends SSE to user immediately. Max 1 direct message per worker per task.

WorkerToManagerCommunication.summary: Two-way communication between workers and managers during task execution. Workers post progress, help requests, and clarifications. Manager responds by writing to workspace or creating follow-up items.

_steps.what: AgentManager wires agent.onProgress callback before sendEvent(). Agent.sendEvent() spawns claude -p --continue --resume.

_tags: @gotcha("If no progress in 10s, heartbeat fires with 'Still working...' message.")
_steps.what: Tool use detected via stream-json line-buffer parsing. onProgress fires. SSE chat_progress event sent to browser showing tool name and arguments.
Agent completes. relayOutputToUser() sends SSE chat_message event with threadId. ThreadStore saves message with collected activity logs.
Gateway use-sse.ts listens for chat_message and chat_progress events. Dispatches as pando-chat-message CustomEvent. Chat page renders activity as collapsible details with color-coded tool use.

RealtimeProgressRelay.summary: How manager output streams to the user in real-time via SSE. Agent.onProgress fires on tool use, relayOutputToUser sends final response.

_steps.what: Builder agent creates frontend code (HTML/CSS/JS). Manager calls POST /projects/:id/deploy.

_tags: @gotcha("Agents NEVER touch GitHub credentials. Node handles all GitHub operations internally.")
_steps.what: Node pushes code to GitHub via contributed code_repository resource. Repo created under token owner (pando-lux).

_tags: @gotcha("Tries up to 3 compute peers. On all fail, returns error.")
_steps.what: Node discovers compute peer via CapabilityRegistry (filter: storageBackend=mongodb). Sends pando/deploy-app P2P message to compute peer.
EC2 compute peer clones from GitHub (public repo, no auth needed). Injects gateway URL into HTML files as window.PANDO_GATEWAY_URL script tag.

_tags: @gotcha("Nodes NEVER upload to S3 directly. ALL deploy operations go through EC2 via P2P.")
_steps.what: EC2 uploads static files to S3: s3://pando-deployments/public/<projectId>/. Returns S3 website URL.
Node updates ProjectRegistry with live URL, deploymentStatus, deployPeerId. Syncs to network via GossipSub. Manager reports URL to user.

AppHostingTier1.summary: Tier 1 deployment: static app files (HTML/CSS/JS) deployed to AWS S3 via EC2 compute peer. API calls route through Gateway Resource Proxy for database access. Near-zero cost.

_steps.what: Builder agent creates frontend + backend code (Express/Fastify server). Manager calls POST /projects/:id/deploy.
Node pushes code to GitHub. Discovers compute peer via CapabilityRegistry P2P discovery.

_tags: @gotcha("detectTierFromCode(appDir) can override manager tier hint. Self-healing tier classification.")
_steps.what: EC2 compute peer clones from GitHub. Runs npm install, npm start on assigned port. Tier auto-detected from code signals: package.json with scripts.start, server framework deps (express, fastify, socket.io).
Backend process started behind nginx reverse proxy. Environment variables injected: MONGODB_URI, S3_BUCKET, PORT. App served at http://<publicAddress>/apps/<projectId>/.
Node constructs URL using profile.publicAddress. Updates project record: deploymentUrl, deployPeerId, deploymentPort. Syncs to ProjectRegistry.
Manager reports URL to user. deployPeerId stored on project for undeploy routing.

AppHostingTier2.summary: Tier 2 deployment: full server deployment on EC2 compute instance. For apps needing persistent backend (WebSockets, real-time, custom backend logic). App served via nginx reverse proxy.

_steps.what: Manager analyzes app requirements: does it need real-time? WebSocket? Custom backend?
If NO to all: Tier 1 (S3 + Resource Proxy). Static content, CRUD apps, read-heavy dashboards all use Tier 1.

_tags: @gotcha("Tier auto-detection at deploy time can override manager hint. Code signals (express, fastify, socket.io, scripts.start) determine actual tier.")
_steps.what: If YES to any: check if cloud_compute resource available via GET /resources?type=cloud_compute. If available: Tier 2 (EC2). If not available: build as Tier 1 with polling fallback.
Deploy to S3 via EC2 P2P. Near-zero cost.
Deploy to EC2 via P2P. EC2 instance runtime + bandwidth billed to resource contributor.

AppHostingTierDecision.summary: How managers decide between Tier 1 and Tier 2 deployment. Default is Tier 1. Tier 2 only when app genuinely requires real-time or custom backend.

_steps.what: User sends build request via chat. Doorman classifies intent and tier (1=S3 static, 2=EC2 compute). Tier stored in Project record at creation time.

_tags: @gotcha("Preflight auto-assigns code_repository alongside storage_db. Agents never assign resources manually.")
_steps.what: Create project with POST /projects. Run preflight (POST /projects/:id/preflight) to auto-assign ALL needed resources: storage_db + storage_blob + code_repository. No manual resource discovery needed.
Manager spawned for project. Manager spawns builder. Builder writes code in workspace. Builder calls POST /projects/:id/deploy when done.

_tags: @gotcha("Agents never see GitHub credentials. Node handles all GitHub operations via POST /projects/:id/github/push internally.")
_steps.what: Node pushes code to GitHub via contributed code_repository resource. Repo created under token owner personal account. Agents NEVER use gh CLI or any local GitHub auth.
Node discovers compute peer via CapabilityRegistry (storageBackend=mongodb). Sends pando/deploy-app P2P message. Tries up to 3 peers.

_tags: @gotcha("Tier auto-detection via detectTierFromCode(appDir) can override manager hint. Self-healing tier classification.")
_steps.what: EC2 compute peer clones from GitHub. Tier 1: uploads static files to S3 with gateway URL injection. Tier 2: npm install, npm start, nginx reverse proxy.
Node updates ProjectRegistry with live URL, deployPeerId, status. Syncs to network via GossipSub. User gets working URL.
App visible in gateway marketplace. Gateway /projects page shows: name, description, tier badge, live URL, GitHub link, health status, deploy timestamp.

AppPlatformArchitecture.summary: Phase 70 complete design for how Pando hosts, deploys, and serves user-built applications. Three-layer credential isolation: Agent Process, Node Process, EC2 Instance. GitHub is source of truth for code. All deploy operations go through EC2 via P2P.

_tags: @gotcha("CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY and PANDO_STORAGE_URL stripped from agent child process environment.")
_steps.what: Layer 1 (Agent Process): HAS workspace, Bash, HTTP API calls. CANNOT see CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY, access S3/MongoDB/AWS, access other workspaces, or launch infrastructure.

Layer 2 (Node Process): HAS GitHub token (fine-grained, reversible). DOES push/pull GitHub repos, send P2P deploy commands, coordinate agents. CANNOT access S3 directly, MongoDB directly, or AWS infrastructure.

_tags: @gotcha("GitHub token is fine-grained PAT: Contents Read/Write only. Cannot delete repos or change org. Damage is reversible via git revert.")
_steps.what: Layer 3 (EC2 Instance): HAS S3 credentials, MongoDB credentials, Resource Proxy. DOES upload to S3, host apps, proxy DB access, clone public repos. CANNOT push to GitHub, run agents, or be accessed by humans.

AppPlatformCredentialIsolation.summary: Three-layer credential isolation model. Agent Process (Layer 1) has workspace only. Node Process (Layer 2) has GitHub token only. EC2 Instance (Layer 3) has S3/MongoDB/AWS credentials.

_tags: @gotcha("Router DECIDES. Node.js EXECUTES simple things. Claude Code BUILDS complex things. Three tiers for cost control.")
_steps.what: Message arrives. Router (ONE OpenAI gpt-4o-mini call, stateless, $0.001) classifies intent and picks route. Router is the DOORMAN: gets you into the right room, then gets out of the way.
For simple actions: Node.js glue handles directly (check balance, transfer Lux, create task entry). Zero AI cost, instant.
For complex actions: Claude Code session with Manager role. Manager plans, delegates, reviews. Builder builds code. QA tests. Same tool, different system prompts.

_tags: @gotcha("project-state.md is a FILE that NEVER compresses. Manager reads at session start, writes at session end. All critical decisions live here.")
_steps.what: Manager reads project-state.md (external brain) at session start. Designs 3-11 step workflow per task. Creates todo items. project-state.md survives context compaction, crashes, months of inactivity.

_tags: @gotcha("Workers are autonomous, not dumb executors. They follow their own todo, report bugs found outside scope, and update genome for what they changed.")
_steps.what: Workers are full Claude Code sessions with own todo list: UNDERSTAND, PLAN, BUILD, TEST, UPDATE_GENOME, REPORT, REFLECT. Workers report discoveries. Workers update genome files. Workers can talk to users via bridge.
QA Agent runs Playwright + API tests after every milestone. Updates genome with test results and known issues. Tracks regression. For simple projects, Manager does QA itself.
Manager reviews worker output, verifies quality. Commits code. Updates genome docs. Reports to user. REFLECT step: what went well, what went wrong, update templates for next project.
Project delivered. Workspace persists for future enhancements. project-state.md updated. Any manager on any node can pick up this project cold by reading CLAUDE.md + project-state.md + manifest.

ArchitectureCapabilities.summary: Master blueprint for how Pando handles every type of user interaction. Three brains (Router/Node.js/Claude Code), four actors (Router/Manager/Builder/QA), project-state.md as external brain, bridge queue as unified communication channel.

_tags: @gotcha("Bottleneck is 10 DIFFERENT projects per node, not users per project. Sequential within a project is correct.")
_steps.what: At 10 users: bridge is SQLite. At 100 users: same architecture, more nodes. 1 node handles ~10 projects with ~10 managers.
At 1000+ users: swap bridge for Kafka. Topic sharding for GossipSub. Delegated voting for governance. Manager hierarchies. Market-based routing.
The actors do not change. The flow does not change. The rules do not change. Upgrade building blocks, not architecture.

ArchitectureScaling.summary: How the architecture scales from 10 to 100,000 users. Pattern: Message to Bridge to Manager to Workers to Bridge to Output. Swap building blocks (SQLite to Kafka), not architecture.

_tags: @gotcha("Default is CONVERSATION. Never accidentally creates projects. TASK patterns: build me, create a, implement, deploy, fix the, add a feature.")
_steps.what: User message arrives at POST /chat/message. detectTaskIntent(message, conversationHistory) returns task or conversation.

If task: generate projectId from message (slugify + timestamp). Manager creates project via POST /projects. Spawns project-specific manager agent with own workspace. CLAUDE.md built via 4-layer template. Thread metadata stores projectId for routing continuity.

Manager agent IS the project AI partner. Asks clarifying questions (scope, hosting, features). Checks user balance via GET /status. Determines project type: personal (checks balance), public (POST /governance/propose, wait for approval), admin (proceeds directly).

_tags: @gotcha("For public projects, governance approval is required before building begins.")
_steps.what: When ready to build: POST /tasks with title, description, priority. Manager designs workflow, approves, dispatches to Scheduler. Workers build in isolated workspaces.

User subsequent messages route to same project manager via thread projectId. POST /chat/threads/:id/message looks up thread projectId, routes directly to project-<projectId> manager. --continue --resume maintains full context.
Tasks complete, pipeline commits, deploy. Claude Code reports back to user in same conversation. Project workspace and session persist for future enhancements.

ChatToProject.summary: How a user natural language request becomes a managed project with a persistent AI partner. Intent detection, project creation, Claude Code session start, and ongoing conversation via thread routing.

_steps.what: PERSONAL: Claude Code checks balance, estimates cost. Sufficient: hold payment via PaymentGate.holdPayment(). Insufficient: inform user, no task created.
PUBLIC: Claude Code proposes to governance. Approved: budget allocated from NETWORK account. Rejected: inform user, suggest alternatives.
ADMIN: no payment check. Tasks created directly using own resources.
Escrow held, released on completion, refunded on failure.
Network-funded project proceeds after vote.
Admin project proceeds immediately.

ChatToProjectPayment.summary: Payment integration for chat-to-project flow. Personal projects check balance. Public projects use governance budget. Admin projects skip payment.

_steps.what: Worker completes task in sandbox (~/.pando/workspaces/{taskId}/). Writes structured report to output/RESULT.md. Scheduler enqueues task_completed to Bridge Queue.
Manager picks up task_completed from bridge. Follows remaining todo list steps.
REVIEW: Manager reads worker output (RESULT.md, changed files). Assesses quality: correct? complete? safe? If bad: create fix task or retry with feedback.
APPLY: Manager copies changed files from workspace to main repo. For trusted tasks, worker may have committed directly.
BUILD: Manager runs npm run build. If build fails: investigate, fix, or create fix task.

_tags: @gotcha("Guardrails are always active. They cannot be bypassed by any agent.")
_steps.what: GUARDRAILS: Safety enforcement always active. No immutable kernel files modified, no protected paths touched, no dangerous patterns. Not optional.

_tags: @gotcha("Manager is the ONLY committer. No other agent commits directly. This eliminates the old TD-25 conflict between pipeline and manager.")
_steps.what: COMMIT: git add <changed files> && git commit -m 'descriptive message'. Commit message includes task ID and summary.

_tags: @gotcha("DOCS step is mandatory for code tasks. This replaced the old standalone pipeline that had no genome update step.")
_steps.what: DOCS (genome update): Manager reads output/graph.json to find affected component docs. Updates genome/knowledge/ .know files, output/graph.json (query: > status). Commits genome changes together with code.
REPORT: commit hash, files changed, genome updated. If deploy needed: Manager requests graceful restart. If build or guardrails failed: rollback via git checkout or DeployManager.restoreFromBackup().

CODE_PIPELINE_FLOW.summary: How code changes move from worker output to committed, tested, documented code. Now part of the Manager workflow, not a separate pipeline system. Manager is the ONLY committer.

_steps.what: Agent completes work in workspace. ContentPublisher extracts content from workspace output. Raw content ready.
ContentSafetyReviewer runs 5-category scan: harmful content, malicious code, OWASP vulnerabilities, Two Laws violations, dependency vulnerabilities. Safety score 0-1. Below threshold: rejected.
ContentRegistry creates SQLite record: title, description, type, tags, creator, content hash, version, safety score. Revenue split: 40% host, 40% builder, 20% NETWORK.
GossipSub publishes to pando/content topic. All nodes receive and store the content record. Version-wins merge for updates. Network-wide visibility.
Content accessible via API: GET /content/:id. Full-text search: GET /content/search?q=... Gateway /content page shows browseable catalog.
ContentMaintenance runs periodic checks: staleness detection (no updates in X days), broken link detection. Auto-creates maintenance tasks for stale content.
Inactive content archived after configurable period. Archived content still accessible but not actively maintained. Clean catalog.

ContentLifecycle.summary: How content is created, verified, published, and maintained on the network. Covers safety review, registration, GossipSub broadcast, serving, maintenance, and archival.

_tags: @gotcha("Code and infrastructure workflows MUST include a DOCS step (genome update). This is mandatory.")
_steps.what: Manager pulls ONE item from Bridge Queue. Assesses it. Designs a workflow: code tasks get plan/spawn/review/commit/docs/report. Research tasks get scope/search/analyze/report/deliver. Each task type gets its own workflow.
Manager declares workflow via POST /managers/:id/workflow with steps array. Each step has id and name. Creates todo items for each step.

_tags: @gotcha("Todo list is the SINGLE source of truth for workflow progress. It survives context compaction because it is a tool, not memory.")
_steps.what: Manager works through todo list. Reports step progress via POST /managers/:id/step. If context compacts during --continue: checks todo list to know where it left off.
Gateway shows workflow progress: each step with status (done, active, pending). User sees real-time progress of their project.
Last step completed. Manager exits. Bridge watcher checks for next item. If bridge empty: idle at zero cost. Workflows stored in manager state.json, pruned after 24 hours.

DynamicWorkflows.summary: How the manager designs per-task workflows dynamically. Todo list IS the workflow. 3-7 steps designed per task type. Survives context compaction via Claude Code todo tool.

_steps.what: Start node. Verify Ed25519 keypair generated. Identity stored in ~/.pando/identities/{peerId}.json. Session cached in ~/.pando/session.json.
Verify GET /v1/status returns valid peerId. Verify identity file exists on disk. Verify session file is loadable.

E2ETestLayer0Identity.summary: E2E test scenario: node starts and creates Ed25519 identity. Verifies identity file creation, session management, and peer ID format.

_steps.what: Start node A and node B. Node B bootstraps to node A. Verify peer connection established.
Node A creates transaction. Verify node B receives it via pando/transactions GossipSub topic within 5 seconds.
Verify both nodes show each other in GET /v1/peers. Verify ledger sync after reconnect.

E2ETestLayer0P2P.summary: E2E test scenario: two nodes discover each other and exchange messages via GossipSub. Verifies TCP+Noise connection, peer exchange, and topic subscription.

_steps.what: Node A transfers Lux to node B. Verify balance updated on both nodes. Verify transaction in GET /v1/status on both nodes.
Verify relay fee (0.1%) applied. Verify daily cap enforcement. Verify dedup on duplicate transaction.

E2ETestLayer0Ledger.summary: E2E test scenario: ledger operations, transfers, and cross-node sync. Verifies balance consistency across network.

_steps.what: From untrusted node (no MongoDB): create thread via POST /chat/threads. Verify thread persists in MongoDB via EC2 compute peer.

_tags: @gotcha("P2PStorageBackend auto-fails over to next compute peer if primary is down.")
_steps.what: From different untrusted node: GET /chat/threads. Verify thread visible (routed via P2P to MongoDB).
Verify zero 503 errors from untrusted nodes. All CRUD operations work via P2P proxy.

E2ETestLayer1Storage.summary: E2E test scenario: P2P storage proxy. Untrusted node reads/writes data via P2PStorageBackend to EC2 compute node.

_steps.what: Send 'build me an app' via POST /chat/threads/:id/message. Verify project created. Verify manager agent spawned.
Wait for builder to complete. Verify POST /projects/:id/deploy succeeds. Verify deployment URL returns 200.
Verify source pushed to GitHub. Verify project visible in GET /v1/projects. Verify app renders correctly at deployment URL.

E2ETestLayer2Deploy.summary: E2E test scenario: full app deployment lifecycle. Chat to project to deployed app with live URL.

_steps.what: Always listening (near-zero cost): health monitors, user inputs, network events, scheduled triggers, external signals. On event detection, wake Manager with cheap LLM call (~$0.01) to assess if event is worth acting on.
Manager triages event. If not actionable: go back to sleep. If actionable: create tasks, route to Scheduler.
Scheduler handles tasks. Daily rhythm: light daily review (~$0.05), weekly deeper review (~$0.50), monthly audit (~$2-5). Governance decides what gets built.

EconomyMode1.summary: Mode 1: Pando managing itself. Event-driven self-management. The AI manages the network like a nervous system manages a body. Sleeps until something happens, handles it, goes back to sleep.

_steps.what: User describes what they want, pays Lux upfront. Project created.
Network breaks it down, builds it phase by phase via manager + workers.
Network hosts the app on contributed infrastructure (S3 or EC2).

_tags: @gotcha("Key difference from Mode 1: AI does NOT make changes without owner approval. For Pando itself, governance decides. For user projects, the OWNER decides.")
_steps.what: Enters maintenance mode: monitor uptime/errors/performance (always-on, cheap). Auto-fix critical issues. Propose improvements to owner (owner approves/rejects).
Owner requests changes (costs more Lux each time). Owner controls autonomy level, budget, and what gets changed.

EconomyMode2.summary: Mode 2: User-owned projects. Someone pays Lux and describes what they want. Network builds, deploys, and maintains it. Owner controls autonomy level, budget, and changes.

_steps.what: User requests public service (search, content delivery, AI analysis). Network routes to capable node.
Node provides compute/storage/bandwidth. Background agents maintain quality: crawlers index content, quality agents spot-check, security agents scan for vulnerabilities.
Node operator earns Lux for providing resources. Revenue sharing: 40% hosting node, 40% building node, 20% network treasury.

EconomyMode3.summary: Mode 3: Network public services. Services nobody specifically owns, belonging to the network: search, content delivery, AI services, security, discovery. Funded by Lux fees.

_steps.what: PaymentGate estimates cost by tier: free tier (search, status, balance checks), paid tier (task execution, project creation), escrow (Lux held during execution).
Escrow: Lux held during execution, released on completion, refunded on failure. Insufficient balance blocks task creation with explanation.

EconomyPaymentGating.summary: How PaymentGate controls access to services based on Lux balance. Free tier for simple queries, paid tier for compute-intensive work, escrow for task execution.

_steps.what: Node completes verifiable work: task completed by scheduler, uptime epoch reached (10 min), API key contributed, governance proposal accepted, or vote cast. Work proof generated.
EmissionWitness.propose(peerId, workType, workProof) creates emission proposal with Ed25519 signature. Rate limited: 10 proposals/hour per node. Proposal broadcast to peers.

_tags: @gotcha("Anti-spoofing: attestation includes peer ID + timestamp + signature.")
_steps.what: Connected peers receive proposal. Each validates: work proof is legitimate, not duplicate. If valid: peer signs attestation with own Ed25519 key.
Requires 2+ unique peer attestations for quorum. Bootstrap fallback: if network has < 3 nodes, single attestation accepted. 5-minute timeout: if quorum not reached, proposal expires.

_tags: @gotcha("No operator logged in means no rewards. Node operates as relay-only without /login or /register.")
_steps.what: Recipient determined by node.getRewardRecipient(): if operator logged in, operator peerId receives Lux; if no operator, no emission (relay-only). Emission applied to ledger: NETWORK account to recipient. Daily cap enforced: 500 Lux max per node per day. Early multiplier applied.
Emission transaction broadcast via pando/transactions topic. All nodes apply the emission to their local ledger. Network-wide consistency achieved.

EmissionFlow.summary: How new Lux is minted when work is verified. Work is done, emission proposed, peers witness and attest, quorum reached, Lux minted to reward recipient, transaction synced network-wide.

_tags: @gotcha("Git commands timeout after 10 seconds. If git is unavailable, return empty results.")
_steps.what: Git commit lands, or periodic check runs, or manager requests drift detection. GenomeAgent.getRecentCommits() fetches recent git log entries. For each commit: analyzeCommit(hash) extracts changed files via git diff-tree.
mapFilesToComponents(files) matches changed files against component entry fields in genome.yaml frontmatter. Returns ComponentMatch[] with direct matches.
For each matched component, parse frontmatter to get depends_on list. Mark both matched component and its dependencies as potentially affected.

detectDrift() scans ALL components for: missing source files (entry points to deleted file), missing genome .md files (genome.yaml lists file that does not exist), broken dependency references (depends_on points to non-existent component). Returns DriftIssue[] with severity (error/warning).
detectNewFiles() scans packages/node/src/ for .ts files not tracked in any component entry field. These are candidates for new genome component entries.

_tags: @gotcha("Scoped context generation failures are non-critical. Workspace creation proceeds without Layer 8 if it fails.")
_steps.what: Drift issues injected into manager event prompt via buildPromptFromBridgeItem() for task_completed events. Manager decides: update genome (code is right) or fix code (genome is right).

When a task workspace is built, GenomeAgent provides scoped context via getScopedContext(). Injected as Layer 8 in worker CLAUDE.md. Algorithm: match affected files to components, resolve depends_on (1 level deep), keyword-match task description, find related flows and rules. Cap at maxComponents (default 8).

GenomeUpdate.summary: How the Project Genome stays in sync with code reality. GenomeAgent analyzes commits, maps files to components, detects drift, and provides scoped context to workers. Zero cost (all local operations).

_tags: @gotcha("Requires 10 Lux stake to propose. New identities with < 10 Lux cannot propose upgrades.")
_steps.what: Any node creates a proposal via POST /governance/propose {title, description, type}. Types: general, code_upgrade, parameter_change, budget. Proposal synced to all nodes via GossipSub.
Nodes comment on proposals during configurable discussion period. Comments synced via P2P.

Each node casts one vote: approve or reject via POST /governance/vote {proposalId, vote}. Votes weighted by reputation. Min reputation gate: low-rep nodes cannot vote on critical proposals. Votes synced via GossipSub.
Quorum reached OR time expires triggers decision. Standard: 51% majority with 30% quorum. Emergency: 40% quorum, 1-hour vote period. Decision: approved or rejected.
If approved: code_upgrade triggers upgrade-protocol flow, parameter_change applied by manager, general creates task from proposal, budget adjusts budget settings.
Proposer gets 5.0 Lux if approved. Voters get 0.1 Lux each via emission witness. Lux minted for governance participation.

GovernanceCycle.summary: How the network makes collective decisions. Any node proposes, all nodes vote (reputation-weighted), quorum decides, action is taken, and participants are rewarded with Lux.

_steps.what: Navigate to gateway /chat. Login as pando. Send: 'Build me a simple guestbook app where visitors can leave messages. Use a dark theme.' Verify doorman instant response.
Verify doorman classifies as intent=build, tier=1. Monitor GET /agents/tree for project manager + builder. Monitor GET /projects for project creation.
Wait 5-15 min for completion. Navigate to deployment URL. Verify app renders (dark theme, guestbook form). Submit a guestbook entry, verify it persists on reload.
Verify source pushed to GitHub. Verify project visible in gateway /projects. Verify chat thread has full conversation history.

HumanE2ETestTier1.summary: Human-level E2E test for Tier 1 static app (S3 deployment). Full lifecycle: chat message to doorman to manager to builder to S3 deploy to live URL.

_steps.what: Click New Chat. Send: 'Build me a real-time chat room app using WebSockets. Users should be able to pick a username and see messages from others in real-time. Use Express and Socket.io.'
Verify doorman classifies as intent=build, tier=2 (WebSocket keyword). Monitor GET /agents/tree for project manager. Monitor GET /network/capabilities for compute peer.

_tags: @gotcha("Deploy auto-discovers compute peers via P2P CapabilityProfile. No manual instance launch needed.")
_steps.what: Wait 10-20 min. Navigate to EC2 URL. Verify chat room loads. Open second browser tab. Send messages from both tabs, verify real-time delivery.
Verify WebSocket connection works. Verify multi-user chat works across tabs. Verify project status in gateway.

HumanE2ETestTier2.summary: Human-level E2E test for Tier 2 WebSocket app (EC2 deployment). Full lifecycle: chat to doorman to manager to builder to EC2 deploy with real-time functionality.

_steps.what: PandoNode.start() calls AgentManager.start(). AgentManager creates pando-node-mgr Agent (role=manager). Starts Bridge Watcher (event-driven, no timer).

Agent.buildClaudeMd() generates 4-layer CLAUDE.md template: Layer 1 (role principles from genome/templates/manager.md), Layer 2 (project context from project-state.md and scoped genome components), Layer 3 (learned lessons auto-updated from experience), Layer 4 (current task). Writes to ~/.pando/agents/{id}/workspace/.
Agent ready to receive events. No process spawned yet. Zero cost while idle.

Any source enqueues item to bridge: user_request (User via API), task_completed/task_failed (Scheduler), worker_message (Worker mid-task), health_alert (HealthMonitor), governance_decision (Governance).

_tags: @gotcha("Per-event spawn: claude -p --continue --resume <sessionId>. stdin=ignore. Delete CLAUDECODE env var from child process.")
_steps.what: If Manager is idle: item = bridge.next(managerId), spawn claude -p with prompt, --output-format stream-json --verbose --dangerously-skip-permissions --model claude-sonnet-4-6. If sessionId exists: --continue --resume <sessionId>. If Manager is busy: item waits in queue (FIFO within priority tier).

Manager receives single-item event prompt. Follows todo list workflow (dynamic per item type). For code tasks: includes commit + genome DOCS step. Process runs, responds, exits. Session ID captured from first spawn for continuity.
Bridge watcher detects Manager process exit. Sets manager status to idle. If bridge queue has more items, spawn again with next item. If empty, do nothing. Zero cost when idle.

_tags: @gotcha("Bridge queue persisted to disk. Items survive restarts and crashes.")
_steps.what: If Claude CLI not found: status=failed, items stay in queue. If spawn times out (5 min): process killed, item re-queued (max 3 retries). If spawn exits non-zero: warning logged, in-flight item re-queued. Session ID cleared on hard failure.

On node shutdown: AgentManager.stopAll() sends SIGTERM to all child processes, waits 10s, SIGKILL remaining. AgentManager.stop() stops bridge watcher, persists agent state. Bridge queue preserved for restart.

ManagerLifecycle.summary: How a manager session starts, runs, and recovers from crashes. Driven by the Bridge Queue with zero-cost idle. No timers, no polling.

_steps.what: Clone repo, npm install, npm run build. Or use launcher: start-node.command (Mac) / start-node.bat (Windows).
node packages/node/dist/cli.js --port 4001. Or double-click launcher. Node process starts running.

_tags: @gotcha("On subsequent runs, auto-loads existing identity. Only prompts for password if identity is encrypted.")
_steps.what: TUI silently auto-creates identity on first run (no prompts). Ed25519 keypair generated, encrypted with password (PBKDF2 + AES-256-GCM). Stored in ~/.pando/identities/{peerId}.json. Session cached in ~/.pando/session.json.

_tags: @gotcha("Without operator login, node earns no Lux rewards. It operates as relay-only.")
_steps.what: TUI checks for ~/.pando/operator-session.json (auto-login). If found and valid: restores operator state. If not found: node runs as relay-only (no rewards). Operator can /login or /register at any time. On login, node registers itself under user account via POST /auth/me/nodes.
If --bootstrap provided: connect to known peer. If no bootstrap: mDNS discovers local peers. Known-peers from previous sessions are dialed automatically. Auto-connects to EC2 bootstrap by default.

_tags: @gotcha("Nodes behind NAT (home Windows/Mac) connect outbound to cloud nodes. Cloud nodes cannot dial back to NAT nodes. This is expected.")
_steps.what: 5s after first peer connects: receives PEER_EXCHANGE with addresses of other nodes in the network. Dials them to form a full mesh. Re-exchange at 30s and 90s catches late-connecting peers. See flow PeerExchange.
LedgerSync requests missing transactions from peers. GossipSub subscribes to all topics. Transactions applied in order until consistent with network state.
First-time node registration: receives genesis Lux. Early multiplier: accounts 1-100 get 5x, 101-1000 get 3x, 1001-10000 get 2x.
API server listening on --api-port (default 4000). P2P listening on --port. Optional: start gateway, scheduler (--scheduler), monitor (--monitor). Full node operational.

NodeOnboarding.summary: How a new node joins the Pando network. Install, start, create identity, optionally login as operator, connect to peers, sync ledger, receive genesis allocation, and become fully operational.

_tags: @gotcha("Eight GossipSub topics: pando/transactions, pando/tasks, pando/governance, pando/resources, pando/reputation, pando/content, pando/capabilities, pando/prices.")
_steps.what: Node creates a state change (transaction, capability update, governance vote, content record). Publishes to the appropriate GossipSub topic.
All connected nodes receive the message via GossipSub. Each node validates: signature, balance (for transactions), dedup check.
Valid state change applied to local store. Account balances updated for transactions. Content records merged by version. Capabilities refreshed with 15-min TTL.

On reconnect, nodes request missing state since last sync (catch-up). Conflict resolution: transactions dedup by hash, task claiming is First-Claim-Wins with timestamp tiebreak, governance votes are additive, capabilities are latest-wins per node, content uses version-number-wins.

P2PSync.summary: How state replicates across all nodes in the network via GossipSub topics. Covers transaction sync, governance, capabilities, content, and conflict resolution strategies.

_steps.what: Node A creates transaction (transfer or emission). LedgerSync publishes to pando/transactions topic.
All connected nodes receive via GossipSub. Each validates: Ed25519 signature, sufficient balance, dedup by tx hash.
Valid transaction applied to local ledger. Account balances updated. Duplicate transactions silently skipped.
Catch-up on reconnect: nodes request missing transactions since last sync point.

TransactionSync.summary: Specific flow for Lux transaction replication across the network.

_steps.what: AI or human commits a fix, pushes to GitHub. Calls POST /upgrade/propose { description }. Creates governance proposal with current commit hash.
Dev mode (8 or fewer active peers): governance auto-approves instantly. Live mode (>8 peers): nodes vote, supermajority (>66%) required.

_tags: @gotcha("Build timeout: 180s. If build fails, automatic rollback to previous commit.")
_steps.what: Proposing node runs git pull, verifies commit hash matches governance-approved hash, npm run build, restart.
After successful local upgrade, broadcasts upgrade_available notification via GossipSub pando/upgrades topic. Includes commitHash, description.
Each peer receives notification, runs git pull, verifies commit hash, builds, restarts. Restart exit code 75 signals PM2/launcher to restart.

_tags: @gotcha("No single point of failure. Even if proposer dies after governance approval, all peers eventually catch up.")
_steps.what: Catch-up timer runs every 5 minutes (30s startup delay). Scans governance for passed upgrade proposals not yet applied. If proposer went offline before broadcasting, peers still discover and apply the upgrade independently.
All nodes running new code. Version-pinned nodes refuse upgrade. Emergency rollback available via POST /upgrade/rollback (fast-track governance vote).

P2PUpgrade.summary: P2P self-upgrade protocol (Phase 82). AI or human commits fix, pushes to GitHub, proposes upgrade via governance, all nodes pull + verify + build + restart. Catch-up timer ensures no node misses an upgrade.

_tags: @gotcha("identify protocol takes 1-3s to complete. updateKnownPeer is delayed 3s to ensure peerStore has announce addresses before persisting.")
_steps.what: New peer connects via bootstrap or known-peers dial. libp2p identify protocol runs automatically, exchanging listen/announce addresses. Announce addresses (public IPs) are stored in the peerStore.

_tags: @gotcha("EC2 nodes in the same VPC connect via internal IPs (172.31.x.x). Without peerStore addresses, known-peers would only store internal IPs that external nodes cannot dial.")
_steps.what: updateKnownPeer() saves both connection addresses AND peerStore announce addresses to ~/.pando/known-peers.json. This ensures public IPs are persisted even when the actual TCP connection uses internal/VPC IPs.

5s after connect: node sends PEER_EXCHANGE message to the new peer. Payload contains all connected peers' addresses (connection addrs + known-peers + peerStore announce addrs). Filtered to exclude the recipient's own address.

_tags: @gotcha("Nodes behind NAT (home Windows/Mac) cannot be dialed from cloud nodes. They connect outbound. This is expected — peer exchange helps them discover cloud nodes, not the other way around.")
_steps.what: Receiving node parses peer list, skips already-connected peers, tries to dial each unknown peer using the shared addresses. Tries all addresses for each peer until one works.
Delayed re-exchange at 30s and 90s after boot broadcasts the full peer list to all connected peers. This catches peers that connected after the initial 5s exchange window.

Combined with known-peers persistence (7-day TTL, 50-peer cap), peer exchange ensures full mesh formation within ~90s of boot. On restart, known-peers are dialed immediately, providing instant reconnection.

PeerExchange.summary: Peer exchange protocol — nodes share peer addresses on connect so new nodes can form a full mesh without a central hub. Replaces the need for a relay/bootstrap hub.

_steps.what: Every 5 minutes, select a random connected peer.

_tags: @gotcha("With fewer than 6 peers, GossipSub mesh may be too thin for reliable message propagation. This timer ensures governance decisions reach all nodes regardless.")
_steps.what: Request governance catch-up from the selected peer. Peer sends all proposals/votes/decisions the requesting node hasn't seen.
Apply received governance state. This catches upgrade proposals, votes, and decisions that were missed via GossipSub.

GovernanceReSync.summary: Periodic governance re-sync — every 5 minutes, nodes request governance state from a random peer. Safety net for thin GossipSub meshes where votes/decisions may not propagate.

_tags: @gotcha("P2PStorageBackend means ThreadStore, ProjectStore, etc. always initialize. No more 'if (!threadStore) return 503'.")
_steps.what: Create P2PStorageBackend implementing StorageBackend interface (6 methods). Finds compute peers via CapabilityRegistry (storageBackend=mongodb). Forwards operations via P2P request-reply (pando/storage-proxy). Failover: tries next compute peer on timeout.
In node startup: if PANDO_STORAGE_URL set, use MongoStorageBackend. If not set, use P2PStorageBackend (instead of leaving null). Every node gets a StorageBackend.
Remove CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY and PANDO_STORAGE_URL from untrusted nodes (Lightsail, Windows). Restart. Node auto-uses P2PStorageBackend.
Test ALL features from untrusted node: search, governance, chat threads, projects. Verify zero 503 errors.

_tags: @gotcha("Agent work happens on untrusted nodes. Data lives on EC2. Real-time via BridgeQueue AND persistent via P2PStorageBackend.")
_steps.what: Full agent workflow E2E from untrusted node with Claude Code: chat message triggers project, manager agent spawns locally, builds something, messages persist to MongoDB via P2P, close/reopen browser confirms history intact.
POST /projects/:id/deploy tries all running EC2 instances, not just first. On timeout/failure, tries next instance.

_tags: @gotcha("Only thing that dies with a node is the agent workspace (ephemeral). Everything else is in MongoDB, GitHub, S3, or P2P-synced.")
_steps.what: Kill one EC2. Verify P2PStorageBackend routes to survivor. Chat and project reads still work. Redeploy goes to surviving EC2. Bring original back, network self-heals.

Phase83Hardening.summary: Phase 83: Network hardening and compute failover. Transform from dev mode (all nodes have everything) to two-tier trust (untrusted nodes use P2PStorageBackend, compute nodes have MongoDB). Every user-facing feature must work from an untrusted node.

_steps.what: Chat messages and project records: MongoDB via P2PStorageBackend. Survives node crash and EC2 death (MongoDB is external). Agent workspace: local filesystem (ephemeral). Does NOT survive node crash.

_tags: @gotcha("The workspace is reconstructable from GitHub. That is the key design principle.")
_steps.what: Project code: GitHub (survives everything). Deployed apps: S3 Tier 1 survives EC2 death, Tier 2 needs redeploy. Ledger/governance: P2P-synced (survives everything). Credentials: MongoDB + master key on EC2 only (survives EC2 death via external MongoDB).

Phase83DataPersistence.summary: Data persistence layers in the hardened network. What survives node crashes and EC2 failures.

_tags: @gotcha("Non-node-operators can contribute too: log into gateway, paste API key, earn Lux when resource is used.")
_steps.what: Provider registers via gateway (POST /resources/register) or TUI (/contribute). Provides resource type, credential, usage limits, pricing. Gateway sends to compute node with CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY.

_tags: @gotcha("Credentials NEVER in P2P messages, NEVER in GossipSub, NEVER in SQLite, NEVER in logs or error messages.")
_steps.what: Compute node encrypts credential with AES-256-GCM + master key + random nonce. Stored in MongoDB pando_credentials collection.
Node creates ResourceRecord (metadata only): resourceId, type, userId, grantedTo, usage limits, pricing, status. NO credentials in the record.
Metadata broadcast via GossipSub pando/resources topic. All nodes learn about available resources (type, status, limits). Credentials only in MongoDB.

As usage is metered by ResourceMeter, emission witness protocol verifies usage. Lux minted from NETWORK account to provider. Rates: 2x API cost for API keys, per-GB-hour for storage, per-request for gateway/compute.

ResourceContribution.summary: How anyone contributes resources (API keys, MongoDB, S3, cloud accounts) to the Pando network and earns Lux. Two-tier trust model: credentials encrypted in MongoDB on compute nodes, metadata-only P2P sync.

_steps.what: Node needs a resource (e.g., AI key for search query). Checks if it is a compute node (has CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY) or user node.
If compute node: decrypt credential from MongoDB via CredentialStore. Call API directly, return result.

_tags: @gotcha("User nodes NEVER see credentials. Only results returned via P2P.")
_steps.what: If user node (no master key): find compute node via CapabilityRegistry (credentialAccess: true). Send P2P request. Compute node decrypts key, calls API, returns answer only.
ResourceMeter records usage: peerId, resourceId, type, units, timestamp.
ResourceMeter records usage on the compute node that performed the operation.
Provider rewarded via emission witness flow.

ResourceUsage.summary: How a node uses a contributed resource. Compute nodes decrypt credentials directly. User nodes route via P2P to compute peers.

_steps.what: Provider calls POST /resources/:id/revoke or /revoke <resourceId> in TUI.
ResourceRecord status set to revoked. Broadcast via GossipSub. All nodes stop using this credential immediately.
Outstanding usage metering finalized. Final Lux payment issued to provider.

ResourceRevocation.summary: How a provider revokes a contributed resource. Immediate network-wide effect.

_tags: @gotcha("Capabilities are a bitmask, not a type. A node can offer multiple resource types simultaneously.")
_steps.what: Node auto-detects hardware capabilities on startup: check for Claude Code, API keys, GPU, storage, public IP. Builds CapabilityProfile with resource types: relay, api_keys, compute_cpu, compute_gpu, storage, gateway, validator, index.
Profile broadcast on pando/capabilities GossipSub topic. Re-broadcasts on change (API key added, disk space changes). Heartbeat every 5 minutes to confirm availability.

Peers store received profiles in SQLite capabilities table with 15-min TTL. Queryable: find all nodes with compute_gpu and vram >= 8GB. Nodes without capability declaration treated as full capability (backward compatible).

ResourceNetworkCapabilityDeclaration.summary: Phase A: Nodes declare capabilities on startup, broadcast via GossipSub, peers store with TTL. Scheduler checks before claiming tasks. Fixes blind-claim failures.

_steps.what: Remove nodes that do not meet requiredCapabilities. Remove nodes over budget. Remove quarantined nodes (SecurityMonitor).

_tags: @gotcha("If local node qualifies and scores within 20% of best: prefer local to avoid network latency.")
_steps.what: Score remaining nodes: reputation_score * 0.4, availability_score * 0.3, price_score * 0.2, latency_score * 0.1. Select highest-scoring node.
Scheduler calls resourceRouter.canExecuteLocally(task). If false, calls resourceRouter.findBestNode(task) to get remote peerId. Task forwarded via P2P.
Remote node scheduler picks up the task. Auto-disable on failure: N consecutive failures marks capability as degraded then disabled. Task reassignment to next capable node.

ResourceNetworkSmartRouting.summary: Phase B: Given a task with requirements, ResourceRouter finds the best node to execute it using scoring algorithm.

_steps.what: Track actual usage: relay bandwidth (libp2p byte counters), API calls (intercept at call sites), CPU compute (task duration + token count), GPU compute (GPU utilization * time), storage (disk usage scan), gateway (request count).

_tags: @gotcha("Metering alone is not trustworthy. A node could lie. Witness verification is required for reward minting.")
_steps.what: Node submits ResourceClaim with evidence. Relay: peer connection logs. Compute: task completion hash. Storage: content retrieval confirmed by requester. API: response hashes.
2+ peers must attest the claim before Lux is minted. If claim cannot be verified, no reward (fail-safe).

ResourceNetworkMetering.summary: Phase C: ResourceMeter accurately measures resource usage per node. Combined with witness verification for anti-gaming.

_steps.what: Nodes set prices in Lux per resource unit. Default pricing provided as baseline. Nodes can charge less than default for essential services, not more.
Prices broadcast via pando/prices GossipSub topic. Latest-wins per resource.

_tags: @gotcha("Each capability has its own adoption curve. A node can be 5x for GPU and 2x for relay simultaneously.")
_steps.what: Router picks cheapest node above floor that meets requirements. Early multiplier per capability type: first 10 nodes get 5x, 11-100 get 3x, 101-1000 get 2x.

ResourceNetworkMarketplace.summary: Phase D: Dynamic pricing based on supply/demand. Nodes set their own prices. Network finds cheapest node meeting requirements.

_steps.what: Source enqueues item to Bridge Queue. Item waits for Manager.
Bridge Watcher spawns Manager with a single item. Manager assesses work type, designs dynamic workflow (3-7 steps), declares workflow via POST /managers/:id/workflow, creates todo items.
POST /tasks to create task, POST /tasks/:id/approve to approve. Manager exits. Task enters approved queue for Scheduler.

Scheduler polls approved queue, routes to AgentManager. AgentManager spawns worker Agent with its own workspace at ~/.pando/agents/{agentId}/workspace/. Worker CLAUDE.md built via 4-layer template: role principles, project context, learned lessons, task description.

_tags: @gotcha("All sessions use --model claude-sonnet-4-6 configurable via DEFAULT_CLAUDE_MODEL.")
_steps.what: Spawns claude -p with workspace CLAUDE.md. Worker follows its own todo list: understand, do the work, post progress messages to bridge, write structured report to output/RESULT.md, exit.

_tags: @gotcha("Two-way communication during execution. Manager can write to worker workspace at manager-response.md.")
_steps.what: Worker can post progress, help_request, clarification, or blocked messages via POST /tasks/:id/messages. Messages route to bridge queue of task Manager. Manager picks them up and responds.
Worker exits. Scheduler reads exit code and workspace output. Enqueues task_completed or task_failed to Bridge Queue.

_tags: @gotcha("Manager is the ONLY committer. No other agent commits code directly.")
@gotcha("DOCS step is mandatory for code tasks: read genome.yaml to find affected components, update genome/knowledge/ .know files.")
_steps.what: Bridge Watcher spawns Manager with task_completed item. Manager follows remaining todo: REVIEW output, APPLY changed files from workspace to repo, BUILD (npm run build), COMMIT (git add + git commit), DOCS (check genome drift, update affected genome files), REPORT summary. Manager exits.

TaskExecution.summary: The primary flow: how work gets done on the Pando network. A trigger enqueues to Bridge Queue, Manager designs a dynamic workflow, creates and approves a task, Scheduler routes to AgentManager which spawns a worker, worker executes in sandbox, Manager reviews and commits.

_steps.what: User starts typing on /chat or clicks New Chat. First message sent. Thread created with auto-generated title (first 50 chars, cleaned). Thread saved to MongoDB via StorageBackend and cached in local SQLite.

detectTaskIntent() returns task or conversation. classifyComplexity() returns simple, medium, or complex. If TASK: thread becomes project thread (type=project). CLAUDE.md written with enriched context. Claude Code session started with --continue.
If CONVERSATION: thread stays as chat (type=conversation). Simple/medium handled by keyword/OpenAI. Complex handled by Claude Code in thread workspace.

_tags: @gotcha("MongoDB is source of truth. SQLite is a local read cache only. Write pattern: MongoDB-first (awaited) then SQLite cache.")
_steps.what: Every message includes threadId. POST /chat/threads/:id/message. Message written to MongoDB (awaited) then SQLite cache. Dispatched to appropriate handler. Response written to MongoDB then SQLite. SSE notification pushed.
Same write pattern. Simple messages use keyword match. Medium messages use OpenAI with conversation history.
User clicks old thread in sidebar. Gateway fetches GET /chat/threads/{id}/messages. Shows full message history. User types new message.

_tags: @gotcha("--continue from workspace may fail if Claude Code cache expired. In that case, start fresh session with memory.md context.")
@gotcha("No StorageBackend (no MongoDB) = user data endpoints return 503.")
_steps.what: If project thread: Claude Code runs with --continue from workspace (session resume). If conversation thread: classified fresh each time. On startup: loadFromBackend() hydrates SQLite cache from MongoDB.

ThreadedChat.summary: How the chat system provides a ChatGPT-like threaded conversation experience. Every conversation is a thread. Threads persist in MongoDB. Project threads route to per-project managers. Conversation threads use keyword/OpenAI tiers.

_steps.what: Node commits code, pushes to GitHub. POST /upgrade/propose { description } creates governance proposal with commit hash. Proposal synced to network.

_tags: @gotcha("Auto-approve threshold is configurable. Default: 8 active peers.")
_steps.what: Dev mode (8 or fewer peers): auto-approve instantly. Live mode (>8 peers): supermajority vote required. Decision: approved or rejected.

_tags: @gotcha("Build timeout: 180s. Restart exit code: 75 (PM2/launcher detects and restarts).")
_steps.what: Proposing node goes first: git pull, verify commit hash matches governance-approved hash, npm run build, restart. Version-pinned nodes refuse upgrade.
After successful local upgrade, broadcasts upgrade_available notification via GossipSub pando/upgrades topic to all peers.

_tags: @gotcha("If build fails on any node, automatic rollback to previous commit via git reset --hard. Emergency rollback via POST /upgrade/rollback.")
_steps.what: Each peer receives notification, runs git pull, verifies commit hash, builds, restarts. Catch-up timer (every 5 min) scans governance for missed upgrades if broadcast was missed.

UpgradeFlow.summary: How the network evolves its own code safely. Node commits and pushes, proposes upgrade via governance, dev mode auto-approves or live mode votes, all nodes pull + build + restart.

_tags: @gotcha("Returning users with projectId skip doorman entirely via thread metadata lookup.")
_steps.what: Message arrives at POST /chat/message or POST /chat/threads/:id/message. API server validates auth. If request includes projectId, routes directly to project manager (skip doorman).

Check body.tier parameter from gateway. tier=medium routes to doormanChat (multi-turn with last 20 messages as history, OpenAI gpt-4o-mini). tier=complex or build routes to project manager. tier=simple or undefined routes to doormanClassify.

_tags: @gotcha("Doorman costs ~$0.001 per classification. Keyword matches are free and instant.")
_steps.what: doormanClassify(message): deterministic keyword matching first (balance, status, peers, help). If no keyword match, OpenAI gpt-4o-mini classifies intent. Returns simple, question, build, or project.
SIMPLE: keyword match answers directly (free, instant). QUESTION: doorman answers via OpenAI (no project created). Both return response immediately.
BUILD intent detected. Create project via POST /projects, run preflight (auto-generates API key, assigns MongoDB). Spawn per-project manager agent: project-<projectId>.
Message enqueued as user_request to project manager bridge queue. AgentManager bridge watcher picks it up. PaymentGate checks escrow if enabled.

_tags: @gotcha("Per-event spawn pattern: claude -p --continue --resume <sessionId>. stdin=ignore, CLAUDECODE env var deleted.")
_steps.what: Agent.sendEvent(prompt) via claude -p --continue --resume. Manager reads message, decides action: conversation (responds directly), task request (designs workflow, spawns workers), or status query (reads node APIs). Real-time progress via onProgress callback to SSE chat_progress.
relayOutputToUser(output, threadId) sends SSE chat_message event to browser. ThreadStore saves message to MongoDB.
Response delivered. All messages stored in ThreadStore (MongoDB-backed). Manager sessions use --continue --resume for conversation continuity.

UserChat.summary: How users interact with the node via natural language. Doorman (OpenAI gpt-4o-mini) classifies intent and routes messages. Simple queries get instant answers. Build requests create projects and spawn per-project managers (Claude Code). Returning users with projectId skip the doorman.

_steps.what: POST /chat/threads/:id/message carries optional tier body parameter: simple (Quick, ~$0.001), medium (Smart, multi-turn OpenAI), complex/build (Full, $0.50-5 Claude Code manager).
simple: stateless doorman keyword/OpenAI. medium: doormanChat with last 20 messages as history. complex: routes to per-project Claude Code manager agent.

UserChatTierRouting.summary: Tier-based message routing within the chat system. Gateway UI sets tier parameter to control cost and capability.

_steps.what: User sends message (e.g., 'I want to build a social app'). Doorman (OpenAI, instant) classifies as build request.

_tags: @gotcha("If Tier 2 requested but no EC2 instances available: tell user, offer Tier 1 alternative. Never silently downgrade.")
_steps.what: Creates project via POST /projects. Runs preflight (auto-assigns MongoDB, generates API key). Classifies tier: static (Tier 1 S3) or backend needed (Tier 2 EC2). Spawns project manager.
Project manager reads CLAUDE.md (template + project context). Designs approach (3-7 steps). Spawns workers: builder, tester, QA as needed. Monitors progress.
Deploys when ready. Reports back to user with live URL.
User has working app. Project visible in gateway marketplace.

UserJourneyNewUser.summary: How Pando handles a new user from first contact through project delivery. Doorman handles fast classification, creates project, spawns manager, manager delivers results.

_steps.what: Check if user is known (session/cookie/account). If YES: look up their projects from MongoDB ProjectStore. Determine which project and which node owns it.

_tags: @gotcha("Priority order: 1) same node, same manager, same session (best). 2) same node, new manager session. 3) different node, new manager. 4) brand new.")
_steps.what: Is owning node alive? YES: route message to that node project manager. NO: reassign project to healthy node.
New node clones from GitHub (has full source code). Spawns new project manager. Manager reads project-state.md + last N thread messages from MongoDB. Continues conversation seamlessly.
Work continues. project-state.md is the external brain. Thread history is the conversation log. Claude Code session is ephemeral. Any manager on any node can pick up any project cold.

UserJourneyReturningUser.summary: How a returning user reconnects to their project. Session lookup, node routing, project resume from GitHub + MongoDB.

_tags: @gotcha("Sequential within one project is correct. You do not want parallel managers on the same project making conflicting decisions.")
_steps.what: All users messages for project route to same project manager via bridge queue. Manager handles all users sequentially per bridge event.
Manager prioritizes: production bugs > blockers > feature requests. Bridge FIFO within priority tier.
Bottleneck is 10 DIFFERENT projects per node (each gets own manager), not 5 users on one project.

UserJourneyMultiUser.summary: How multiple users collaborate on a single project. All users route to same project manager. Sequential processing per bridge event.

_tags: @why("Used in applies_to for universal agent rules like the Two Laws and todo-loop pattern.")
AllAgents.summary: All agent entities in the system: Agent, AgentManager, and any spawned worker/manager instances.

_tags: @why("Used in applies_to for node-level invariants like Law II (survive) and health protocol rules.")
AllNodes.summary: All node instances running the Pando software: PandoNode and its subsystems.

_tags: @why("Used in applies_to for Law I (do not harm) which applies to every service without exception.")
AllServices.summary: All service modules across kernel, core, and platform layers.

_tags: @why("Used in applies_to for rules that have zero exceptions, like the three-bucket data residency test.")
AllComponents.summary: Every component in the Pando architecture — used for universal architectural rules like data residency.

_tags: @why("Referenced as enforced_by in todo-loop and other agent behavioral rules — templates are the enforcement mechanism.")
AgentTemplates.summary: The 6 role-specific agent templates (manager, builder, tester, reviewer, researcher, devops) that define agent behavior via CLAUDE.md injection.

_tags: @why("Referenced in governance-tiers.know to distinguish project-level vs network-level governance scope.")
ProjectTypes.summary: Project type classifications: private (owner-only), shared (collaborators), and public (network-visible). Determines governance scope and revenue distribution.

_tags: @why("Flow steps reference Manager as the actor performing coordination. Maps to an Agent instance with the manager template.")
Manager.summary: The Manager agent role — coordinates projects, spawns workers, maintains project-state.md, and is the only committer. Used as actor in flow steps.

_tags: @why("Flow steps reference Gateway as the user-facing entry point for messages and interactions.")
Gateway.summary: The Pando Gateway web UI — Next.js frontend that connects to a node via HTTP API. Used as actor in flow steps where the user interacts through the web interface.

_tags: @why("Flow steps reference TUI as the actor for interactive terminal operations like identity creation and peer connection.")
TUI.summary: The Terminal User Interface entry point for running a Pando node interactively. Used as actor in onboarding flows.

_tags: @why("Flow steps reference CLI as the actor for automated/scripted node startup.")
CLI.summary: The non-interactive CLI entry point for running a Pando node. Used as actor in onboarding flows.

_tags: @why("Flow steps reference TestRunner as the generic actor performing test execution. Concrete implementation varies by test type.")
TestRunner.summary: Conceptual test execution actor in flow steps — maps to QaRunner for automated tests and human testers for manual E2E scenarios.

_tags: @why("Before this rule, the scheduler auto-approved tasks, auto-spawned QA, called the Planner, and made autonomous decisions. This caused rogue agents, duplicate work, and cascading failures.")
AUTHORITY_MODEL.rule: Only Managers create and approve tasks. Workers execute. Scheduler allocates resources. No other actor may create, approve, or decide on tasks.

_tags: @why("Managers are the decision-makers. They determine what work is needed and approve it for execution. Scheduler handles the logistics of spawning.")
MANAGER_AUTHORITY.rule: Manager CAN: create tasks, approve tasks, make decisions, commit code. Manager CANNOT: spawn workers directly (delegates to Scheduler).

_tags: @why("Scheduler is a pure executor. Limiting its authority to spawning approved tasks prevents autonomous decision-making that caused cascading failures.")
SCHEDULER_AUTHORITY.rule: Scheduler CAN: spawn workers for approved tasks only. Scheduler CANNOT: create tasks, approve tasks, make decisions, commit code.

_tags: @why("Workers are sandboxed executors. Any authority beyond task execution creates escape vectors for cascading side effects.")
WORKER_AUTHORITY.rule: Workers execute their assigned task and nothing else. They CANNOT: create tasks, approve tasks, spawn agents, make decisions, commit code.

_tags: @why("Autonomous monitor actions caused rogue restarts. Monitor observes, Manager decides, Scheduler executes.")
MONITOR_AUTHORITY.rule: HealthMonitor is a data source only. It CANNOT: create tasks, approve tasks, spawn agents, make decisions, commit code.

_tags: @why("Multiple enforcement layers ensure the authority model cannot be circumvented by any single bypass.")
AUTHORITY_ENFORCEMENT.summary: Enforced by: Scheduler constructor rejecting Planner parameter, worker CLAUDE.md restricting tool access (--disallowedTools), API endpoints requiring managerId for task creation, Guardrails blocking workers from POST /tasks.

_tags: @why("Without budget limits, a runaway project could consume all network resources. Budget enforcement ensures fair resource distribution across projects.")
BUDGET_ENFORCEMENT.rule: Every project has a daily Lux budget. When exhausted, the manager defers non-critical work until the next period.

_tags: @why("Multiple budget layers (total, per-node, per-project) prevent any single entity from monopolizing Lux emission or spending.")
BUDGET_LIMITS.rule: Hard cap: 10B Lux total supply. Daily cap per node: 500 Lux. Default project budget: 100 Lux/day. Relay fee: 0.1% per transfer.

_tags: @why("Pre-spawn budget checks prevent over-spending before it happens. Period-based resets keep the system flowing without manual intervention.")
BUDGET_ENFORCEMENT_MECHANISM.summary: ManagerAgent.checkBudget() validates before every session spawn. ProjectSettings tracks budgetLuxLimit and budgetLuxSpent per period. resetBudgetIfNeeded() auto-resets at period boundary. EmissionWitness requires 2+ peer attestations.

_tags: @why("Node operators can trivially modify code to capture credentials. Untrusted nodes must never see plaintext credentials.")
TWO_TIER_TRUST.summary: Untrusted user nodes never receive credentials — they route requests via P2P to trusted EC2 compute nodes that hold the CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY and can decrypt from MongoDB.

_tags: @why("Random amateurs, non-technical users, and potentially malicious actors run nodes. A node operator can trivially add console.log to capture any credential.")
NO_PLAINTEXT_CREDENTIALS_ON_USER_NODES.rule: User-run nodes NEVER receive, store, or see credentials. Only EC2 compute nodes with CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY can decrypt.

_tags: @why("Log files are often accessible, backed up, or transmitted. Any credential in logs is a credential leaked.")
NO_CREDENTIALS_IN_LOGS.rule: Never log a credential, even partially. Use [REDACTED] or the resource ID.

_tags: @why("P2P messages are received by all nodes including untrusted ones. Credentials in P2P messages would be exposed to every participant.")
NO_CREDENTIALS_IN_P2P.rule: GossipSub broadcasts resource METADATA only (type, status, owner, grantedTo). Never encrypted credentials, never wrapped keys.

_tags: @why("Minimizing the time credentials exist in memory reduces the attack window for memory dumps or process inspection.")
CREDENTIAL_WIPE_AFTER_USE.rule: After a query completes on a compute node, the decrypted credential MUST be discarded from memory.

_tags: @why("Compromised credentials must be invalidated network-wide immediately. Delayed revocation leaves a window for misuse.")
INSTANT_REVOCATION.rule: When /revoke is called, ALL nodes mark resource as revoked within seconds via GossipSub. Compute nodes also revoke in MongoDB.

_tags: @why("Scoped credentials limit blast radius if a credential is compromised despite all other protections.")
MINIMUM_PRIVILEGE.rule: Contributors should create scoped credentials (e.g., MongoDB read/write to pando db only).

_tags: @why("Separating public project identity from personal developer identity prevents accidental credential or history leakage.")
PUBLIC_CODE_IDENTITY.rule: All public Pando code pushed under pando-lux GitHub identity. Never personal accounts.

_tags: @why("Git history is permanent and public. Secrets committed to git are effectively leaked forever.")
NO_SECRETS_IN_GIT.rule: CredentialStore (MongoDB) is the ONLY place for secrets. Never in git history, config files, or source code.

_tags: @why("The master key is the root of the credential trust chain. Any leak of the master key compromises all encrypted credentials.")
MASTER_KEY_HYGIENE.rule: CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY is never committed to source code, never in config files, never in logs. Only in environment variables on admin machines and EC2 instances.

_tags: @why("AES-256-GCM provides authenticated encryption. Unique nonces per credential prevent cross-credential analysis attacks.")
ENCRYPTION_DESIGN.summary: Master key is random 256-bit (64 hex chars). Per-credential encryption uses AES-256-GCM with a unique random nonce. MongoDB stores: encryptedCredential (base64), nonce (base64), type, userId, status, metadata.

_tags: @why("Separating storage proxy from credential operations ensures that even if storage proxy is compromised, credentials remain isolated.")
STORAGE_PROXY_SEPARATION.summary: P2PStorageBackend (pando/storage-proxy) handles user data CRUD. CredentialStore (pando/credential-op) handles credential decryption. The pando_credentials collection is blocked from the storage proxy.

_tags: @why("Agents run arbitrary AI-generated code. Exposing master key or storage URL to agents would allow credential exfiltration.")
AGENT_CREDENTIAL_ISOLATION.rule: CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY and PANDO_STORAGE_URL are stripped from agent child process environment variables.

_tags: @why("Before this rule, HealthMonitor had executeRecoveryActions() and executeRecovery() that auto-restarted services and auto-killed processes. Autonomous recovery caused more problems than it solved.")
HEALTH_MONITOR_DATA_ONLY.rule: HealthMonitor collects data ONLY. It does NOT make autonomous decisions, execute recovery actions, or trigger any side effects.

_tags: @why("A toggle could be accidentally or maliciously flipped. Removing the code entirely eliminates the risk.")
NO_MANAGER_MODE_TOGGLE.rule: All setManagerMode() toggles are deleted. HealthMonitor is ALWAYS data-only. No toggle exists to re-enable autonomous action.

_tags: @why("Separation of observation from action. The Manager reads monitor data and makes informed decisions. The monitor never acts on its own.")
HEALTH_MONITOR_SCOPE.summary: HealthMonitor collects metrics (CPU, memory, disk, network), detects patterns (failure rates, performance trends), generates alerts (threshold breaches, anomalies), and exposes data via API for the Manager to read and decide.

_options.reason: Autonomous recovery caused rogue restarts and cascading failures. StrategyLoop, SelfImprover, and AutoUpdater were entirely deleted. Manager reads data and decides.
Auto-restarting services and auto-killing processes without Manager oversight was unpredictable and harmful.

AUTONOMOUS_RECOVERY_REMOVAL.problem: Should HealthMonitor autonomously recover from failures, or should it be data-only with the Manager making recovery decisions?

_tags: @why("Without this rule, user data gets trapped on individual nodes, breaking durability, portability, and multi-user access.")
THREE_BUCKETS_RULE.rule: Every piece of data in Pando belongs to exactly one of three buckets: User Data (MongoDB), Network State (SQLite + P2P GossipSub), or Node-Local (local filesystem). No exceptions.

_tags: @why("If a node burns down, no user loses anything they care about. MongoDB is the durable source of truth for all user-generated content.")
USER_DATA_BUCKET.summary: User Data lives in MongoDB via StorageBackend. Includes: projects, threads, messages, collaborators, invites, transfers, deployments, ratings, reports, revenue, distributions, subscriptions, contributions, scores. Survives node death.

_tags: @why("Network state must be replicated to all nodes for decentralized consensus. P2P GossipSub provides this without central coordination.")
NETWORK_STATE_BUCKET.summary: Network State lives in SQLite + P2P GossipSub replication. Includes: accounts (with username, password_hash), transactions, emissions, governance, capabilities, content registry, reputation, resources. Rebuilds from peers after node death.

_tags: @why("Operational data that is specific to a single node instance. Loss on node death is acceptable because it can be regenerated or is ephemeral.")
NODE_LOCAL_BUCKET.summary: Node-Local data does not sync and is disposable. Includes: auth-local.db (key store), identity keys, agent workspaces, logs, metrics, monitor audit trail, guardrails config, task file locks, known-peers cache.

_tags: @why("This simple test prevents architectural mistakes where data ends up in the wrong bucket.")
DECISION_TEST.rule: If a node burns down and a user loses something they care about, it belongs in MongoDB. If other nodes need it, it belongs in P2P. If nobody else needs it, it is local.

_tags: @why("MongoDB is the source of truth. SQLite is a read-performance cache. Writing to cache first could lose data if the MongoDB write fails later.")
MONGODB_PRIMARY_WRITE_ORDER.rule: Write order is MongoDB FIRST (awaited), then SQLite cache update. If MongoDB write fails, the operation fails. No silent data loss.

_tags: @why("Graceful degradation. A node without storage can still participate in the P2P network but honestly reports that it cannot serve user data.")
NO_STORAGE_NO_USER_DATA.rule: Nodes without MongoDB (no StorageBackend) return 503 Service Unavailable for all user data endpoints. P2P features (ledger, governance, resources) still work.

_tags: @why("Auth must work across all nodes without central database. P2P-synced ledger and stateless JWTs achieve this with cryptographic verification.")
AUTH_DATA_LOCATION.summary: Auth data (username, password_hash, is_claimed) moved from MongoDB to P2P-synced ledger accounts table in Phase 56. Sessions replaced by stateless JWTs signed by each node's Ed25519 key in Phase 86. No session storage anywhere.

_tags: @why("Early networks are practically centralized even if nominally decentralized. Without automatic transitions, governance can vote to remain centralized because the only voters are centralized.")
DECENTRALIZATION_PROTOCOL.summary: Automatic, non-negotiable governance transitions based on unique human operator count. Transitions happen by math, not by consensus. Four milestones: Bootstrap (<10), Emerging (>=10), Established (>=100), Decentralized (>=1000).

_tags: @why("During bootstrap, the founder operates most nodes. Veto prevents malicious early joiners from hijacking the network before it has enough honest participants.")
MILESTONE_0_BOOTSTRAP.rule: Below 10 unique human operators: founder node (FOUNDER_NODE_ID) retains veto on Tier 1 and Tier 2 proposals. Veto does NOT apply to Tier 3 or Tier 4. Standard quorum still required.

_tags: @why("10 independent operators provide enough diversity to eliminate the need for founder veto. Council diversity prevents governance capture by a single operator.")
MILESTONE_1_EMERGING.rule: At 10+ unique human operators: founder veto on Tier 1-2 drops automatically. Council diversity rule activates (max 1 seat per operator). Founder votes with weight equal to reputation score.

_tags: @why("At 100 operators, 15% cap means one operator needs 7 others to form a majority. Prevents any single actor from unilaterally controlling governance.")
MILESTONE_2_ESTABLISHED.rule: At 100+ unique human operators: no single operator may hold more than 15% of total network reputation weight. Enforced at vote-tallying time before votes are counted. Applies to ALL operators including founder.

_tags: @why("The most significant event in the network's history. The founder relinquishes all special governance privileges. Cannot be undone without Tier 1 vote (90% quorum).")
MILESTONE_3_DECENTRALIZED.rule: At 1000+ unique human operators: FOUNDER_NODE_ID constant is cleared from governance.ts. Founder becomes just a node with no special rules. This event is broadcast as DECENTRALIZATION_COMPLETE via GossipSub.

_tags: @why("Operator count is the most important governance metric. Inflation moves to an unearned milestone; deflation delays necessary transitions. Accuracy is essential.")
