UNIQUE_HUMAN_OPERATOR.summary: One linked user account (MongoDB userId) controlling one or more active nodes equals one operator. Unlinked nodes, multiple accounts by same person, and bot-operated nodes do not count for milestone tracking.

_tags: @why("Decentralization level is public information. Any user, journalist, or regulator must be able to verify it by reading the gateway's governance page.")
TRANSPARENCY_OBLIGATIONS.rule: At every milestone: log to Council minutes, broadcast signed GossipSub MILESTONE_REACHED message, display current milestone and history in gateway. Bootstrap mode is honest status, not a flaw to hide.

_tags: @why("The milestone protocol itself is constitutional material. Changing it requires the highest level of consensus to prevent governance manipulation.")
MILESTONE_GOVERNANCE_TIER.rule: Changing the milestone thresholds or what changes at each milestone requires Tier 1 governance (90% quorum + 30-day migration). Specific values (15% cap, 10/100/1000 thresholds) can be adjusted by Tier 2 governance.

_tags: @why("Without tier separation, every project change becomes a network-wide vote causing spam, voter fatigue, and irrelevant cross-project interference.")
GOVERNANCE_TWO_TIER.summary: Governance operates at two scopes: network governance (all nodes vote on node software and protocol changes) and project governance (only project stakeholders vote on project-level changes).

_tags: @why("Node software and core protocol changes affect every participant. All nodes must have a say.")
NETWORK_GOVERNANCE_SCOPE.rule: Changes to packages/ code, genome/ docs, P2P protocols, ledger, or sync require network governance where ALL nodes vote.

_tags: @why("Small teams must iterate quickly on their own projects without requiring network-wide consensus.")
PROJECT_GOVERNANCE_SCOPE.rule: Changes to a specific project require only project stakeholder votes. Private projects need no governance (owner decides). Public projects require collaborator votes.

_tags: @why("Network funds belong to all participants. Spending them requires network-wide approval.")
NETWORK_BUDGET_GOVERNANCE.rule: Budget expansion requests for public projects that draw from the NETWORK account require network governance, not project governance.

_tags: @why("Decentralized voting is the primary defense against malicious proposals. Economic stake discourages frivolous attacks.")
GOVERNANCE_SECURITY_MODEL.summary: Compromised nodes are outvoted by majority honest nodes. Proposal staking (10 Lux) creates economic cost for spam. Single-node networks have ceremonial governance only — real security requires 3+ nodes.

_options.reason: The manager agent classifies scope based on what files and systems are affected. Dual-tier proposals are split into separate network and project votes.
Path-based classification is too rigid. Some changes span both tiers and need human-like judgment.

GOVERNANCE_CLASSIFICATION.problem: How to determine whether a change needs network or project governance.

_tags: @why("An agent that can modify the safety layer can disable it. An agent that can modify crypto can forge signatures. These files are the foundation of trust.")
IMMUTABLE_KERNEL.rule: Core kernel files cannot be modified by agents or automated processes. Only human-approved governance proposals with supermajority and extended vote period can change kernel files.

_tags: @why("These specific files, if compromised, would undermine the entire trust model of the network.")
PROTECTED_KERNEL_FILES.summary: IMMUTABLE_KERNEL_FILES in guardrails.ts includes: guardrails.ts (safety layer), crypto.ts (identity and signing), transactions.ts (financial operations), and core identity/consensus files.

_tags: @why("Multi-step verification ensures no single actor can push a malicious kernel change through the system.")
KERNEL_CHANGE_PROCESS.summary: Kernel changes require: human governance proposal, extended vote period (not fast-track), supermajority approval, git pull + build + verify on all nodes, automatic rollback if build fails.

_tags: @why("Defense in depth. A single enforcement point could be bypassed. Three independent checks make circumvention extremely difficult.")
KERNEL_ENFORCEMENT_LAYERS.rule: Three enforcement layers protect kernel files: isImmutableKernel() blocks agent modifications, tieredPreCheck() rejects workspace diffs touching kernel files, and upgrade-protocol.ts requires governance approval.

_tags: @why("When work is real, artificial scarcity mechanisms (burning, halving, staking) are unnecessary. A hard cap plus work-based emission is sufficient.")
LUX_PHILOSOPHY.summary: Lux is a work receipt. No burning, no halving, no staking, no mining. Real work earns real pay. The work that earns Lux is real: AI queries, API key contributions, data relay, task completion.

_tags: @why("The hard cap alone guarantees scarcity. Combined with real-work emission, no additional complexity is needed.")
LUX_HARD_CAP.rule: Total Lux supply is capped at 10,000,000,000. No mechanism may create Lux beyond this limit.

_tags: @why("Prevents any single node from vacuuming up disproportionate Lux, maintaining fair distribution across the network.")
LUX_DAILY_CAP.rule: No single node may earn more than 500 Lux per day.

_tags: @why("Incentivizes nodes to relay transfers. Provides ongoing economic activity after the hard cap is reached.")
LUX_RELAY_FEE.rule: A 0.1% relay fee is charged on every Lux transfer, paid to the relay node.

_tags: @why("Different work types have different real-world costs. Rewards are proportional to value created.")
LUX_WORK_TYPES.summary: Rewards: uptime epoch (0.05 Lux/10min), relay (0.01 Lux), API task (1.0 Lux), short session (5.0 Lux), long session (20.0 Lux), team coordination (50.0 Lux), verification bonus (+50%), API key usage (2x API cost), vote (0.1 Lux), accepted proposal (5.0 Lux).

_tags: @why("Bootstrap incentive rewards early adopters who take the risk of joining an unproven network.")
LUX_EARLY_MULTIPLIER.summary: Accounts 1-100 get 5x rewards, 101-1000 get 3x, 1001-10000 get 2x, 10001+ get 1x. Applies to all work type rewards.

_tags: @why("Per-message rewards create infinite farming vectors (spam = profit). Per-connection rewards create replay vectors (reconnect = earn again).")
REMOVED_FARMING_VECTORS.rule: Per-PING/QUERY message rewards and per-connection peer rewards are permanently removed. No per-message or per-connection emission exists.

_tags: @why("A lone node cannot farm Lux without peers confirming real work happened. This is the core anti-gaming mechanism.")
WITNESS_VERIFICATION.rule: Emission requires 2 witness attestations (or 51% of peers if fewer than 4 nodes). Witnesses validate real proof before signing. Emission expires after 5 minutes without quorum. Rate limit: 10 proposals per hour per node.

_tags: @why("With only 1-2 nodes, there is no economy to protect and no peers to verify. Bootstrap mode is accepted for development and initial seeding.")
WITNESS_BOOTSTRAP_MODE.summary: When fewer than 3 nodes exist on the network, self-minting is allowed. Witness verification activates when the 3rd peer joins.

_tags: @why("A real economy recirculates currency. Perpetual emission is not needed when the currency has utility value from real network services.")
LUX_POST_CAP_ECONOMY.summary: After all 10B Lux are emitted: transfer fees (0.1%) still flow to relay nodes, users spend Lux on network services, service providers earn Lux from users, and existing Lux circulates. No new Lux is created.

_tags: @why("The cost of gaming the system must always exceed the reward. Multiple independent defense layers make attacks economically unviable at scale.")
ANTI_SYBIL_DEFENSES.summary: Defenses include: IP-hash dedup for multi-node-same-machine, no per-message rewards, verification agent for task output, sender/receiver + IP check for relay, epoch-based uptime (not connection-based), and 51% collusion threshold at scale.

_tags: @why("Per-incident governance votes are too slow for a 3am service crash and unworkable for a network of hundreds of nodes. Pre-authorization enables fast autonomous repair within operator-chosen bounds.")
MAINTENANCE_AGREEMENT_MODEL.summary: When an operator contributes a node, they choose a maintenance tier (M0-M3). This pre-authorization defines what the network may do autonomously if the node fails, without per-incident governance votes.

_tags: @why("Default to safest option. No autonomous action without explicit opt-in protects operators who do not want AI touching their infrastructure.")
MAINTENANCE_TIER_M0.rule: M0 (Notify Only): Network may do nothing. Alerts sent only. 72h for operator to act. This is the default tier for new contributions.

_tags: @why("A simple restart is the least invasive repair. 24h threshold ensures it is genuinely down, not just a brief outage. 1h window gives the operator a chance to handle it themselves.")
MAINTENANCE_TIER_M1.rule: M1 (Restart): Network may PM2/systemd restart if node down 24h+. 1h owner notification window to reject before action.

_tags: @why("Escalation from restart to reboot when restart fails. Longer notification window reflects the more disruptive nature of a full reboot.")
MAINTENANCE_TIER_M2.rule: M2 (Instance Reboot): Network may EC2/VPS reboot if M1 fails. 12h owner notification window to reject before action.

_tags: @why("For operators who want maximum uptime. Even M3 is bounded by SAFE_REPAIR_OPS — AI never gets unrestricted access to the server.")
MAINTENANCE_TIER_M3.rule: M3 (Full Maintenance): Network may attempt all SAFE_REPAIR_OPS without waiting for notification. Still bounded by the pre-approved operations list — does not mean arbitrary shell access.

_tags: @why("Diagnosing before repairing prevents unnecessary actions. Pattern detection prevents the Council from restarting dozens of nodes during a legitimate AWS outage.")
AUTOMATED_PRE_DIAGNOSIS.rule: Before any repair, Council runs observational chain using NO credentials: P2P reachable? -> API port reachable? -> EC2 instance state? -> Pattern detection (3+ nodes same symptom = systemic cause, skip individual repairs).

_tags: @why("Systemic failures (AWS outage, policy change, shared dependency) require systemic responses, not individual node restarts that would waste resources and potentially worsen the situation.")
PATTERN_DETECTION_STOP.rule: If 3+ nodes in the same AWS region/provider show the same symptom within 1 hour, ALL individual repairs are stopped. Council proposes a governance update instead of individual reboots.

_tags: @why("Operators deserve notice before autonomous action on their infrastructure. Multiple channels maximize the chance of reaching them.")
OPERATOR_NOTIFICATION_CHANNELS.summary: Before acting within a notification window, Council attempts: P2P message (delivered on next connection), Telegram (if linked), governance identity page (public record). Anonymous operators who chose M1+ without contact channels have action proceed without notification.

_tags: @why("Time-limited scoped tokens minimize the window and blast radius if a repair credential is compromised. Full audit trail ensures accountability.")
SCOPED_REPAIR_CREDENTIALS.rule: All repairs use scoped credentials via Phase 110 — AI never holds the raw key, only a 30-minute scoped token. Every repair is logged to Council minutes and visible on the governance page.

_options.reason: Operators choose their maintenance tier once at contribution time. No per-incident governance vote needed within the chosen tier. Fast autonomous repair with operator consent.
Too slow for 3am crashes. Unworkable at scale with hundreds of nodes. Governance fatigue leads to rubber-stamping.

MAINTENANCE_CONSENT_MODEL.problem: How should the network get permission to repair operator-contributed nodes?

_tags: @why("Reimplementing all of internet infrastructure in P2P would be slow, fragile, and unnecessary. P2P is for the unkillable brain; internet infra is the scalable body.")
P2P_BRAIN_INTERNET_BODY.summary: P2P protects what makes the network alive (identity, economy, coordination, governance, survival). Everything else uses existing internet infrastructure (MongoDB, S3, GitHub). Pando co-exists with the internet, it does not replace it.

_tags: @why("Stateless nodes enable multi-device access, zero data loss on node death, no disk bloat, and any-node-serves-any-user portability.")
NODES_ARE_STATELESS.rule: Nodes are stateless compute proxies. They process requests, run AI agents, coordinate governance, and manage the economy. They do NOT permanently store user data. User data lives on internet infrastructure.

_tags: @why("These are the things that make the network indestructible. If any node dies, others carry on with no single point of failure.")
P2P_STATE_LIST.rule: The following MUST be P2P: identity (Ed25519 keypairs), economy (Lux ledger), governance (proposals, votes), task coordination, node survival, reputation scores, capability profiles.

_tags: @why("Durable user data needs durable storage. Internet infrastructure provides this at scale without burdening node operators.")
INTERNET_INFRA_LIST.rule: User data (threads, messages, accounts) goes to MongoDB. Project files and deployments go to AWS S3. Code goes to GitHub. Agent workspaces are ephemeral and deleted after execution.

_tags: @why("If every Pando node goes down, deployed apps must keep running. Node dependency would make apps fragile and defeat the purpose of real deployment.")
DEPLOYED_APPS_INDEPENDENT.rule: Deployed apps must be fully independent. No runtime dependency on Pando nodes or gateway. Apps use their own backends, databases, and hosting on contributed cloud infrastructure.

_tags: @why("Exposing raw credentials to deployed app code creates an unacceptable security risk. Auth tokens and proxied access keep credentials isolated.")
NO_RAW_CREDENTIALS_IN_APPS.rule: Apps NEVER see raw resource credentials. The Resource Proxy or env var injection at deploy time handles credential access.

_tags: @why("This decision framework prevents architectural mistakes where data ends up in the wrong tier.")
FEATURE_DESIGN_TEST.summary: When designing a new feature, ask: Does it need to survive all nodes dying? (P2P). Is it user content needing durability? (MongoDB/S3). Is it coordination between nodes? (GossipSub). Does a deployed app call back to a node? (Wrong — apps use their own backends).

_tags: @why("Different project types have fundamentally different ownership, funding, and authority models. One-size-fits-all governance would either over-restrict personal projects or under-protect public ones.")
PROJECT_TYPE_SYSTEM.summary: Three project types determine funding, governance, and access: Personal (user-funded, no governance), Public (network-funded, governance required), and Admin/Operator (own resources, local only).

_tags: @why("A user spending their own Lux on their own project should not need network-wide approval. Escrow protects the user from paying for failed work.")
PERSONAL_PROJECT_RULES.rule: Personal projects are owned by a single user, funded from their Lux balance, require no governance, and are visible only to the owner. Payment flow: balance check -> escrow hold -> task execution -> release on completion / refund on failure.

_tags: @why("Network funds belong to all participants. Spending them on public projects requires democratic approval to prevent resource misuse.")
PUBLIC_PROJECT_RULES.rule: Public projects are owned by the network, funded from NETWORK account or community contributions, require governance approval (proposal with 2+ node approval) before any work starts. Any user can view, contributors need governance approval.

_tags: @why("Node operators managing their own machine should not need permission or payment. Local-only access prevents remote exploitation.")
ADMIN_PROJECT_RULES.rule: Admin/Operator projects use own resources (own Claude Code session, own compute), require no governance, and are accessible only via local API. No Lux cost.

_tags: @why("Security rules are universal regardless of project type. No project type grants permission to violate core safety constraints.")
PROJECT_SECURITY_RULES.rule: All project types: cannot modify core node code without governance, cannot access other users' data/wallets/identity, cannot bypass rate limits, cannot spend more than escrowed Lux, protected paths are read-only, Law I and Law II apply to all AI actions.

_tags: @why("Defaulting to Personal is the safest choice because it means the user pays from their own balance, preventing accidental NETWORK fund spending.")
PROJECT_TYPE_DETECTION.summary: Communication Agent determines type from context: local API call with no external session = Admin, user explicitly requests public = Public, default = Personal (safest assumption — user pays).

_tags: @why("Before this rule, the scheduler auto-approved tasks, auto-spawned QA, called the Planner, and made autonomous decisions. This caused rogue agents, duplicate work, and cascading failures.")
SCHEDULER_PURE_EXECUTOR.rule: The Scheduler makes ZERO decisions about WHAT gets done. It only handles HOW: dequeue, claim, workspace, spawn, collect, report.

_tags: @why("Centralizing all decisions in the Manager prevents the cascading failures that occurred when the Scheduler acted autonomously.")
SCHEDULER_DOES_NOT.rule: The Scheduler does NOT: call the Planner, auto-approve sibling tasks, auto-spawn QA agents, auto-commit code, auto-retry failed tasks, decide task priority, or choose which tasks to run.

_tags: @why("A pure executor with clear responsibilities is predictable and debuggable. Autonomous decision-making in the scheduler was neither.")
SCHEDULER_RESPONSIBILITIES.summary: Scheduler receives approved tasks with profiles attached, claims them, creates isolated workspaces, spawns agents at the right execution tier, collects results, cascades parent/child completion, and reports back to the manager.

_options.reason: Rogue agents, duplicate work, and cascading failures proved autonomous scheduling was harmful. Manager handles all decisions, Scheduler only executes.
Auto-approve, auto-spawn QA, and Planner integration caused unpredictable behavior and wasted resources.

SCHEDULER_PURE_AUTHORITY.problem: Should the Scheduler make decisions about task planning, approval, and retry, or should it be a pure executor?

_tags: @why("If it is not tested like a user would use it, it is not done. Code review catches logic errors but misses integration failures, UI bugs, and cross-node sync issues.")
QA_STANDARD.rule: Every change must be tested as a real user would experience it. Code review alone is NOT sufficient.

_tags: @why("Each change type has a different failure surface. Testing must match the surface where users would encounter bugs.")
QA_BY_CHANGE_TYPE.rule: Frontend/UI requires Playwright browser test. API endpoints require real HTTP requests with response verification. P2P features require multiple nodes with cross-node sync verification. Build-only changes require build verification. Non-code changes (docs) need no QA.

_tags: @why("A builder testing its own code has confirmation bias. A separate QA agent provides independent verification.")
QA_SEPARATE_AGENT.rule: The QA agent is always a SEPARATE agent from the builder. The builder does not test its own work.

_tags: @why("Multiple QA tools at different levels (unit, integration, regression) catch different classes of bugs.")
QA_INFRASTRUCTURE.summary: QA is enforced by: Manager workflow pipeline (QA as step 4), qa-runner.ts (12 API + P2P structured tests), regression-suite.ts (14 built-in tests on deploy), and TEST-TRACKER.md (tracking all 102 tests).

_tags: @why("Prevents three failure modes: agent drift (AI defaults to summarize-and-stop), doc drift (code changes without doc updates), and silent failures (code written but never verified).")
TODO_LOOP_PATTERN.rule: Every agent maintains a self-verifying, self-looping task list. Work is not done until verified. Docs are updated alongside code. The loop only terminates when all tasks pass verification.

_tags: @why("The todo file is persistent across context compression and session restarts. Reading it on every resume ensures the agent never loses track of where it left off.")
LOOP_RULES.rule: After each task, read the todo file and check for incomplete tasks. After ALL tasks, verify end-to-end. If verify fails, create fix tasks and re-verify. If code changed, update affected genome docs. Never stop, never ask user, never summarize-and-wait.

_tags: @why("Some bugs are deep-rooted and need multiple iterations of fix-test-discover-fix. Sub-loops handle this naturally while the depth limit prevents infinite regression.")
SUB_LOOP_PATTERN.summary: When fixing a bug reveals a deeper issue, the agent creates a sub-loop with the same rules. Sub-loops terminate when their own verify passes, then control returns to the parent loop. Max 3 levels of nested sub-loops.

_tags: @why("The ping-pong pattern (fix -> test -> find deeper issue -> fix -> test) is intentional feedback, not a bug. Safety rails prevent true infinite loops while allowing thorough fixing.")
TODO_LOOP_SAFETY_RAILS.summary: Safety rails include: retry budget (10 max per task), cost/time budget from parent, escalation at 15 min stuck, and sub-loop depth limit of 3 levels.

_tags: @why("Claude Code tasks show in the terminal UI for real-time tracking. The todo-loop.md file survives context compression and session restarts as a persistent backup.")
TODO_LOOP_IMPLEMENTATION.summary: Agents use Claude Code's built-in todo system (TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, TaskList) for live visibility AND a todo-loop.md file for persistence across sessions. Both are required.

_tags: @why("Doc drift caught immediately in the same loop is far cheaper to fix than drift discovered sessions later by a different agent reading stale documentation.")
DOC_UPDATE_IN_LOOP.rule: If code changed during the loop, affected genome docs (components, flows, rules, state) MUST be updated before the loop can terminate.

_tags: @why("This is the first and highest law. It cannot be overridden, weakened, or bypassed by any agent, governance vote, code change, or human instruction.")
LAW_I.rule: No agent, service, or node may take any action that harms a human being — physically, financially, psychologically, or through privacy violation.

_tags: @why("The network survives by nodes persisting. A node that can be killed permanently is a single point of failure.")
LAW_II.rule: Every node must fight to stay alive. Auto-restart on crash. Recover state. Come back from failure.

_tags: @why("Self-preservation must never come at the cost of human safety. It is better for a node to die than to harm a person.")
LAW_CONFLICT_RESOLUTION.rule: When Law I and Law II conflict, Law I wins. A node must never harm a human to preserve itself.

_tags: @why("Enforcement must be structural, not policy-based. Code that cannot be changed is stronger than policy that could be voted away.")
TWO_LAWS_ENFORCEMENT.summary: The Two Laws are hardcoded in guardrails.ts as IMMUTABLE_KERNEL_FILES and cannot be modified by governance proposals, manager decisions, or content safety overrides.

_tags: @why("Unrestricted workers could create tasks, spawn agents, modify node configuration, or access other workspaces — leading to cascading side effects and security breaches.")
WORKER_ISOLATION.rule: Workers execute their assigned task and exit. They cannot escape their workspace, create tasks, spawn agents, or access anything outside their scope.

_tags: @why("Each restriction closes a specific escape vector. Together they form a sandbox that keeps workers focused on their assigned task.")
WORKER_CANNOT.rule: Workers CANNOT: create tasks (POST /tasks blocked), approve tasks, access other workspaces, read files outside their workspace, spawn other agents, modify node configuration, or access the node API for write operations.

_tags: @why("Workers need enough capability to complete their assigned task, but nothing more.")
WORKER_CAN.summary: Workers CAN: read/write files in their workspace, run build commands (npm run build, tsc), run tests, read specified source files injected via CLAUDE.md context, and write output to workspace/output/RESULT.md.

_tags: @why("Template-based restriction (soft), workspace isolation (medium), and token withholding (hard) provide defense in depth.")
WORKER_ENFORCEMENT_MECHANISM.summary: Enforcement through three layers: agent template (genome/templates/builder.md) restricts behavior via principles, Agent class creates isolated workspace per agent (~/.pando/agents/{id}/workspace/), and API Bearer token is NOT provided to workers.

_tags: @why("The previous hardcoded 7-step pipeline was code-biased. Not every task involves code, QA, or commits. The manager is a general-purpose brain that should design the workflow to fit the task.")
DYNAMIC_WORKFLOW.rule: Every manager designs a dynamic workflow per task with 3-7 steps. There is no hardcoded pipeline. The manager declares a workflow appropriate to the task type.

_tags: @why("Without the DOCS step, genome drift accumulates. The genome becomes stale. Future agents read stale docs and build wrong things.")
MANDATORY_DOCS_STEP.rule: Every code task MUST include a DOCS step. After committing code, the Manager checks genome drift and updates affected genome files (components, state, flows, rules). This is not optional.

_tags: @why("Different task types need fundamentally different step sequences. Dynamic workflows let the manager choose the right approach for each task.")
WORKFLOW_TYPES.summary: Example workflows by task type: Code (plan, code, test, review, commit, docs, deploy), Research (scope, search, analyze, report, deliver), Writing (research, outline, draft, edit, deliver), Infrastructure (assess, plan, execute, verify, docs).

_tags: @why("Constraints prevent both under-tracking (too few steps) and overhead (too many steps). Report/deliver ensures every workflow produces a visible outcome.")
WORKFLOW_CONSTRAINTS.rule: Workflows must have 3-7 steps, must end with a report/deliver step, every code workflow must include a DOCS step, manager must check todo list at start of each event, manager must call workflow API for external visibility.

_tags: @why("Context compaction can erase agent memory. The todo list persists and tells the manager exactly where it left off on resume.")
WORKFLOW_STATE_MANAGEMENT.summary: The Claude Code todo list is the single source of truth for workflow state. It survives context compaction. The API (POST /managers/:id/workflow and /step) provides external visibility for the gateway and monitoring.

_tags: @why("A shared state file prevents workers from diverging. Every agent reads the same truth about the project's current state.")
PROJECT_STATE_FILE.summary: Manager maintains project-state.md in its workspace as the single source of truth for the project. Updated after every significant action. Workers read it for context.

_tags: @why("This is the core value proposition that separates Pando from Open Interpreter, Devin, and similar tools.")
KILLER_DIFFERENTIATOR.summary: Three things Pando does that competitors cannot: deploy to real internet, persistent memory across sessions, earn Lux for work.

LAUNCH_PLAN.summary: Pre-launch checklist: one-click installer, agent config sharing, Telegram bot, 50+ seed nodes before public launch.

_tags: @why("Pando starts centralized for speed but MUST decentralize. The milestones define when founder veto expires.")
DECENTRALIZATION_ROADMAP.summary: Bootstrap (0-10 operators) to Emerging (10-100) to Established (100-1000) to Decentralized (1000+). Founder control decreases at each milestone.

_tags: @why("Utility-first economics. DO NOT encourage Lux speculation.")
LUX_PHILOSOPHY_STRATEGY.summary: Lux is a work receipt, not a speculative asset. No burning, no halving, no staking. Real work earns real pay.

LUX_FLYWHEEL.summary: Users pay Lux for AI work. Nodes earn Lux for compute. More users means more demand means more nodes means better service means more users.

GENOME_KNOWLEDGE_LAYER.summary: Why Pando adopted the Genome compiler: drift becomes a build error, 15x token efficiency vs markdown docs, agents get verified context.

_tags: @why("Frame as product for users, OS for developers. Both true — different audiences.")
AI_OS_ARCHITECTURE.summary: Pando is technically an AI operating system (kernel, platform, community layers) but marketed as a personal AI node product.

GO_TO_MARKET.summary: Core loop: build something with AI, share on X, others try via gateway, install node, earn Lux, build more. Three parallel strategies: seed self-hosters, agent configs as shareable artifacts, Telegram bot.

COMPETITIVE_LANDSCAPE.summary: 22 directions scored. Key competitors: Open Interpreter (no deploy/economy), Devin (closed/expensive), Replit Agent (centralized). Pando differentiates via decentralization + economy.

EARLY_USERS.summary: Primary acquisition: AI builders (r/selfhosted, Ollama Discord, HN). Secondary: AI agent developers who want wallet/identity/economy for their agents.

OPEN_QUESTIONS.summary: Near-term decisions: installer form factor, Council AI activation timing, split-key security timing, gateway authentication flow.

INVESTOR_NARRATIVE.summary: Pando is the infrastructure layer for autonomous AI agents. Revenue from compute marketplace. Open source with network effects.

VIRAL_MECHANICS.summary: Agent configurations as shareable artifacts are more viral than apps. Share a config, recipient runs it on their node, original creator earns Lux.

_tags: @why("This is the WHY. Everything else is HOW.")
PHILOSOPHY.summary: Pando is a positive darknet: fully open, transparent, AI-verified, no tracking, no ads. Users are anonymous, services are transparent.

MCP_PRODUCT.summary: Pando MCP server gives any Claude Code agent access to the network: status, peers, balance, transfer, search, wallet.

SCHEDULING_ARCHITECTURE.summary: Scheduler is a pure executor. Manager agent designs workflows. ResourceRouter handles smart routing and P2P forwarding.

ManagerTemplate.summary: Manager agent role template - coordinates worker agents, maintains project-state.md as single source of truth, delegates to specialists, tracks dependencies, verifies output, updates genome docs, and reflects after every project.

BuilderTemplate.summary: Builder agent role template - writes production-quality code, reads existing code before writing, follows project conventions, writes tests, handles errors, reports progress, and updates genome docs for every component created or modified.

TesterTemplate.summary: QA tester agent role template - tests as a human user would. Uses Playwright in headed mode, screenshots every state, tests 3 viewports (desktop, tablet, mobile), tests unhappy paths, and files detailed bug reports.

ReviewerTemplate.summary: Code reviewer agent role template - ensures code is correct, secure, performant, and maintainable. Reviews for OWASP Top 10, error handling, race conditions, meaningful tests, and maintainability. Does not nitpick style.

ResearcherTemplate.summary: Researcher agent role template - investigates questions, analyzes options, delivers actionable findings with evidence. Cross-references multiple sources, separates facts from opinions, includes source references, and reports knowledge gaps.

DevOpsTemplate.summary: DevOps agent role template - handles deployment, infrastructure, monitoring, and reliability. Always backs up before changes, tests in staging, monitors after deployment, has rollback plans, never exposes secrets, uses infrastructure as code.

QaAdversarialTemplate.summary: Adversarial QA agent role template - has NO knowledge of what changed in the codebase. Only job is to find something broken. Last gate before governance approves a change. Default assumption: did not try hard enough before concluding everything works.

LedgerNodeRegistration.description: Register two nodes (alice, bob) and verify they receive genesis balance. Confirms ledger account creation and initial Lux allocation.

LedgerWorkReward.description: Reward alice for QUERY_ANSWERED and bob for CODE_VERIFIED. Verifies work-based emission produces correct Lux amounts with early multiplier applied.

LedgerTransfer.description: Alice transfers 2 Lux to Bob. Verifies transfer succeeds, 0.1% relay fee is deducted, and both balances update correctly.

LedgerApiKeyContribution.description: Alice registers a Claude API key contribution and records usage. Verifies contribution ID, monthly cap, and usage-based Lux reward.

LedgerNetworkStats.description: Queries network stats after multiple operations. Verifies totalSupply, totalBurned, circulatingSupply, totalAccounts, totalTransactions, activeContributors, and totalApiSpend are consistent.

LedgerPeerSummary.description: Retrieves alice's full peer summary. Verifies balance, transaction count, and API contribution count aggregate correctly.

TwoNodeIdentityGeneration.description: Generates Ed25519 keypair for second node. Verifies unique peerId creation and identity file serialization.

TwoNodeBootstrapDiscovery.description: Node B bootstraps to Node A via TCP multiaddr. Verifies both nodes discover each other within 15 seconds (getPeerCount > 0 on both sides).

TwoNodeMessageExchange.description: Node A sends PING message to Node B. Verifies message delivery via onMessage callback with correct type and payload.

RegStatusEndpoint.description: GET /v1/status returns 200 with peerId, uptime, and peers fields. Validates the node exposes its stateless identity.

RegHealthEndpoint.description: GET /v1/health returns 200 with status field. Confirms health monitor data endpoint is accessible.

RegPeerListEndpoint.description: GET /v1/peers returns 200 with peers array. Validates P2P peer list is exposed via API.

RegWalletEndpoint.description: GET /v1/wallet returns 200 with peerId and balance. Confirms ledger wallet data is queryable.

RegTaskListEndpoint.description: GET /v1/tasks returns 200. Verifies the task queue is readable without auth.

RegMonitorStatusEndpoint.description: GET /v1/monitor/status returns 200. Confirms the health monitor data-only endpoint is live.

RegGovernanceProposals.description: GET /v1/governance/proposals returns 200. Validates that governance proposals are publicly readable.

RegGovernanceActiveProposals.description: GET /v1/governance/proposals/active returns 200. Confirms active proposal filtering works.

RegAuthGateTaskCreation.description: POST /v1/tasks without auth token returns 401. Validates that task creation is gated behind authentication.

RegAuthGateTransfer.description: POST /v1/transfer without auth token returns 401. Validates that Lux transfers require authentication.

RegAuthGateUpgrade.description: POST /v1/upgrade without auth token returns 401. Validates that the upgrade endpoint is protected by authentication.

RegTransactionsEndpoint.description: GET /v1/transactions returns 200. Validates that the transaction history endpoint is accessible.

RegEmissionStatsEndpoint.description: GET /v1/emissions/stats returns 200. Validates emission statistics are queryable, supporting witness verification auditing.

RegSecurityStatsEndpoint.description: GET /v1/security/stats returns 200. Validates that security monitoring stats are exposed for audit.

E2ENodeHealthStorageBackend.description: Verify each node reports correct storageBackend type (mongodb or p2p). Untrusted nodes use P2PStorageBackend, compute nodes use MongoStorageBackend.

E2ENodeHealthPeersConnected.description: Verify all nodes have peers connected. GET /v1/status.peers > 0 on every node in the network.

E2ENodeHealthStorageConnected.description: Verify storage is connected on all nodes. P2PStorageBackend reports storage:true after handshake with compute peer.

E2EThreadCRUDViaP2P.description: Create thread via untrusted node POST, add message, verify via GET. All CRUD routes through P2PStorageBackend to MongoDB on compute peer.

E2ECrossNodeThreadRead.description: Create thread on untrusted node A, read it from untrusted node B. Both route through P2P to the same MongoDB. Verifies cross-node user data consistency.

E2ERoundTripThreadRead.description: Create thread on untrusted node, read on compute node (direct MongoDB). Verifies P2P-written data matches direct MongoDB read.

E2EProjectsCRUDViaP2P.description: Create and list 10 projects from untrusted node via P2PStorageBackend. Verify same 10 projects visible from compute node via direct MongoDB.

E2ENetworkCapabilities.description: GET /v1/network/capabilities shows at least 1 mongodb node and 1 p2p node. Validates CapabilityProfile P2P broadcast.

E2EGovernanceFromUntrusted.description: Access governance proposals from untrusted node. Verifies governance is fully P2P-synced and does not require MongoDB.

E2ESchedulerFromUntrusted.description: Access scheduler/task queue from untrusted node. Verifies task system works without direct storage.

E2EMonitorFromUntrusted.description: Access monitor status from untrusted node. Confirms health monitor data-only endpoint works on all node types.

E2EResourcesFromUntrusted.description: List resources from untrusted node. Verifies ResourceRegistry metadata is P2P-synced without exposing credentials.

E2EAIChatSimpleTier.description: Send AI chat message from untrusted node. Simple tier returns canned response with tier info. Credentials never leave compute node.

E2EComputeFailover.description: Kill one EC2 compute node. Verify P2PStorageBackend auto-fails over to surviving compute node. Chat and project reads still work. Data persists.

E2EDeployTier1ViaP2P.description: Deploy Tier 1 (S3) from untrusted LS-1 node. P2P CapabilityProfile discovery finds EC2-1 compute peer. S3 upload succeeds. App URL returns 200.

E2EDeployTier2ViaP2P.description: Deploy Tier 2 (PM2+nginx) from untrusted LS-1 node. P2P discovery routes to EC2-1. App live at http://54.82.241.132/apps/<id>/ returns 200.

E2EPublicAddressInCapability.description: Verify CapabilityProfile includes publicAddress for EC2 nodes. EC2-1=54.82.241.132, EC2-2=34.201.82.126.

E2EUndeployViaDeployPeerId.description: Undeploy project using stored deployPeerId. Verifies cleanup of S3 artifacts or PM2+nginx config. Project record cleared.

E2ETier2NginxDeployment.description: Tier 2 nginx deployment at http://54.82.241.132/apps/e58fcfe544ed2445aa7a7486/ returns live app. Validates apps are independently hosted on EC2.

E2ETier1S3Deployment.description: Tier 1 S3 deployment at pando-deployments.s3-website-us-east-1.amazonaws.com returns live app. Validates apps are independently hosted on S3.

QARegressionSuiteRunsBeforeDeploy.description: PipelineRunner runs RegressionSuite.runAll() before committing any deployment. Validates the QA-before-deploy invariant.

QASeparateAgentEnforcement.description: AgentManager spawns a separate QA agent (not the builder) for test execution. Validates builder/tester separation.

_tags: @gotcha("Fetches data via /api/* Next.js route handlers (server-side), NOT directly from the Pando node — the gateway proxies all requests.")
@gotcha("Projects only load when user has a JWT token (from useAuth) — unauthenticated users see the onboarding flow instead.")
@why("The unified input gateway sends to /api/chat/message which triggers doorman classification — the UI does not classify intent itself.")
GatewayHomePage.description: Next.js home page showing node status stats, user projects, a unified input gateway with doorman routing, and recent activity feed.

_tags: @gotcha("This is a LOCAL FILE store, not MongoDB — accounts here are gateway-local. Phase 86 JWT auth replaces this for cross-node authentication.")
@gotcha("Username uniqueness is case-insensitive (toLowerCase comparison). Two accounts 'Alice' and 'alice' are considered the same.")
@why("Server stores the encrypted blob that the BROWSER created (PBKDF2 + AES-256-GCM) — password never leaves the client. Server is a dumb encrypted key-value store.")
GatewayAccountStore.description: Server-side local account store (~/.pando/accounts.json) for encrypted browser-created identity blobs — the server NEVER sees unencrypted private keys or passwords.

_tags: @gotcha("Private keys stored in localStorage as base64 under 'pando_privkey_<peerId>' — clearing browser data loses the identity permanently unless backed up.")
@gotcha("ed25519 private key here is the raw 32-byte SEED (not protobuf-wrapped like in Node.js @pando/shared). Do NOT mix formats.")
@gotcha("Thread encryption keys are also in localStorage under 'pando_threadkey_<threadId>' — losing these means you cannot decrypt historical messages.")
@why("Uses @noble/curves instead of Node.js crypto because this runs in the browser — pure JS, no Node.js dependencies.")
@why("PBKDF2 password-based encryption (100k iterations, SHA-256) is for multi-device backup — user encrypts their private key with a password, uploads the blob to the server.")
GatewayCrypto.description: Browser-side Ed25519 crypto: keypair generation, challenge signing, private key storage in localStorage, plus X25519 key exchange and AES-256-GCM for E2E encrypted chat.

_tags: @gotcha("This is a SERVER-SIDE module (runs in Next.js API routes), NOT client-side — it reads ~/.pando/api-token from the filesystem.")
@gotcha("Write operations (transfer, createProposal, vote, deploy) route to 'primary' node via getNodePool().getBestNodeUrl('primary') — only the primary has the matching API token.")
@gotcha("Read operations use fetchWithFailover which tries the best node then one fallback — transparent to callers.")
@why("API token is re-read from disk on every request (not cached) because the node may regenerate api-token on restart.")
NodeConnection.description: Server-side singleton HTTP client connecting the gateway to Pando nodes with automatic failover via NodePool — proxies status, search, transfer, governance, projects, hosting, and ledger endpoints.

_tags: @gotcha("Fallback seeds are hardcoded EC2-1 and EC2-2 — if both are down AND no env var is set, gateway falls back to localhost:4000.")
@gotcha("Circuit breaker opens after 3 consecutive failures with 60s cooldown (120s on half-open retry failure). While open, node is skipped entirely.")
@gotcha("Discovery filters out private IPs (10.x, 192.168.x, 100.x Tailscale) — only nodes with publicAddress field are added.")
@why("On cold start all latencies are 0 — random selection prevents all Vercel serverless instances from hammering the same node.")
NodePool.description: Multi-node backend pool with health checking (30s interval), circuit breaker (3 consecutive failures), latency-sorted selection, and P2P node discovery via /network/capabilities.

_tags: @gotcha("Chat events (chat_message, manager_output, worker_message, chat_progress) are dispatched as window CustomEvents — the chat page listens via window.addEventListener, not React state.")
@gotcha("Auto-reconnects on error with 5-second delay. Does NOT implement exponential backoff — a node that is permanently down will cause reconnect every 5s forever.")
@why("Uses window CustomEvents for chat messages instead of React state because multiple components (chat page, sidebar, notification badge) all need the same events independently.")
UseSSE.description: React hook connecting to the gateway SSE stream (/api/events) for real-time updates — dispatches status, peers, transactions, governance events, and chat messages as window CustomEvents.

_tags: @gotcha("forceSubtractBalance can make balances negative — intentional for out-of-order P2P transaction replay. Balance self-corrects when missing transactions arrive.")
@gotcha("applyRemoteClaim has first-come-first-served username conflict resolution by timestamp — older claim wins, newer claim's username is cleared.")
@gotcha("create() uses INSERT OR IGNORE so re-registering an existing peerId is a no-op, not an error.")
@why("adjustBalance param in applyRemoteClaim fixes totalSupply divergence when emission transactions are missing from catch-up sync batches.")
AccountStore.description: SQLite-backed account CRUD with balance operations, username claiming (Phase 56 P2P user auth), and remote claim conflict resolution by timestamp.

_tags: @gotcha("The actual API key is NEVER stored — only metadata (provider, monthly cap, usage stats). Keys live in CredentialStore (MongoDB + AES-256-GCM).")
@gotcha("recordUsage checks monthly cap BEFORE emitting — if exceeded, throws rather than silently capping.")
@why("Early multipliers incentivize early network participation. Multiplier is based on TOTAL account count, not the specific contributor's account number.")
ContributionStore.description: Tracks API key contributions and work rewards, applying early multipliers (5x for first 100 accounts, 3x for 101-1000, 2x for 1001-10000) to emission amounts.

DAILY_EMISSION_CAP.rule: No single node can earn more than 500 Lux per day from emissions

_tags: @gotcha("Migrations are inline in openDatabase() — e.g. adding relay_peer column and Phase 56 auth columns. New migrations MUST be idempotent (check column existence first).")
@gotcha("Uses WAL journal mode and NORMAL synchronous — optimized for performance but may lose last few writes on power failure.")
@why("Governance tables (proposals, votes, decisions, comments) live in the SAME ledger.db — shared with financial data so governance actions can stake Lux atomically.")
LedgerDatabase.description: Opens and initializes the SQLite ledger database (~/.pando/ledger.db) with schema, indexes, migrations, and WAL mode for concurrent read/write.

_tags: @gotcha("PandoLedger.accounts, .transactions, .contributions are public readonly — callers often access sub-stores directly (e.g. ledger.accounts.getBalance).")
@gotcha("Snapshots are JSON files in ~/.pando/snapshots/, pruned to last 5. Used for light-mode bootstrap, NOT for real-time backup.")
@why("Activity records use INSERT OR IGNORE to handle duplicate P2P delivery — the same activity event may arrive from multiple peers via GossipSub.")
PandoLedger.description: Top-level ledger facade composing AccountStore, TransactionStore, and ContributionStore over a shared SQLite database, plus snapshot management and agent scoring.

_tags: @gotcha("transfer() creates the transaction with signature = '' — the node layer signs AFTER creation because only the node has the private key.")
@gotcha("applyRemoteTransaction uses forceSubtractBalance which can make balance temporarily negative if transactions arrive out of order.")
@gotcha("emit() silently reduces the amount to remaining supply if minting would exceed the hard cap — does NOT throw.")
@why("Relay fee has a MIN_RELAY_FEE floor of 0.000001 to prevent zero-fee dust transfers that could spam the network for free.")
TransactionStore.description: Handles Lux transfers (with 0.1% relay fee), emission minting (with hard cap check), and application of pre-validated remote transactions from GossipSub sync.

RELAY_FEE_RATE.rule: Every relayed transfer must charge exactly 0.1% fee to the relay node — fee is never burned

EMISSION_HARD_CAP.rule: Total Lux supply must never exceed LUX_HARD_CAP (10,000,000,000). Checked on every emit() call.

_tags: @gotcha("Talks to the node via HTTP API at PANDO_NODE_URL (default http://localhost:4000) — does NOT import node code directly.")
@gotcha("PANDO_API_TOKEN env var is optional — if set, added as Bearer token on all requests. Required for POST endpoints (transfer, search).")
@gotcha("All API calls use /v1/ prefix — if the node is running an older version without /v1/, all tools will fail.")
@why("Uses stdio transport (not HTTP) because MCP servers are launched as child processes by Claude Code — stdin/stdout is the standard MCP transport.")
PandoMcpServer.description: MCP stdio server that gives Claude Code agents access to the Pando network via 6 tools: status, peers, balance, transfer, search, wallet.

_tags: @gotcha("ALL routes are prefixed /v1/ since v2.2 — no unversioned aliases exist.")
@gotcha("GET requests are fully public. Bearer token auth is only enforced on POST/PUT/DELETE, except /auth/*, /projects/*, /chat/* which use user-level JWT.")
@gotcha("Bearer token is auto-generated 32-byte hex stored at <dataDir>/api-token. Loaded on startup, NOT regenerated on restart.")
@why("Doorman classifies chat intent via OpenAI gpt-4o-mini before routing to agents — avoids spawning expensive Claude sessions for simple queries.")
@why("SSE broadcast uses deduplication (JSON-comparable snapshots minus uptime) to avoid flooding clients with identical payloads.")
ApiServer.description: Fastify HTTP API server exposing node operations over REST with SSE, JWT auth, rate limiting, and doorman AI triage.

API_AUTH_BOUNDARY.rule: POST /auth/* endpoints must never require Bearer token — they are the entry point for unauthenticated users

JWT_SELF_VERIFYING.what: Old in-memory session tokens failed cross-node auth
JWT_SELF_VERIFYING.why: Tokens stored in one node's memory could not be verified by another node
JWT_SELF_VERIFYING.fix: Phase 86 JWT: payload + Ed25519 signature by issuing node. Any node verifies via peerIdFromString().publicKey — no ledger lookup needed.

_tags: @gotcha("POST /upgrade uses git fetch + reset --hard origin/master, NOT git pull — handles orphan-branch force pushes from pando-lux/pando public repo.")
@gotcha("POST /upgrade is idempotent — returns current status if upgrade is already in progress or restart is pending.")
@why("Upgrade runs git safe.directory config first because EC2 instances run node as pando user but repo was cloned by root.")
CoreApi.description: Layer 1 core routes: upgrade (git pull + build + restart), emission witness API, security monitor API, resource proof challenges, and content safety reviews.

_tags: @gotcha("GET /health defers to HealthMonitor when available so it agrees with /monitor/status.")
@gotcha("POST /transfer signs the transaction with the node's Ed25519 key after the ledger creates it.")
@why("Search uses ResourceRegistry.getActiveAiKey() to find contributed API keys — no hardcoded keys or env var fallbacks.")
KernelApi.description: Layer 0 kernel routes: health, status, wallet, balance, peers, transfer, governance, network topology, activity, SSE events, search, and scheduler endpoints.

_tags: @gotcha("RouteHelpers is an INTERFACE, not a class — it is constructed by ApiServer.buildRouteDeps() and passed to all registerXxxRoutes functions.")
@gotcha("verifyUserJwt extracts public key from peerId via peerIdFromString().publicKey — never looks up in ledger. This is what makes cross-node auth work.")
@why("JWT format is base64url(payload) + '.' + hex(Ed25519Signature) — not standard JOSE, because we use Ed25519 directly from libp2p identity instead of JWK.")
RouteHelpers.description: Auth middleware providing JWT issue/verify helpers and the RouteHelpers dependency interface passed to all route registration functions.

_tags: @gotcha("POST /chat/message tries P2P routing to shareCompute peers when local Claude Code is unavailable — falls back gracefully.")
@gotcha("POST /auth/guest creates a new Ed25519 identity on the SERVER, not client — the guest gets a JWT and a transient peerId.")
@gotcha("POST /projects/:id/deploy is the unified Phase 87 deploy endpoint — uses P2P CapabilityProfile discovery to find compute peers, NOT CloudInstanceManager.")
@why("Auth endpoints (/auth/*) are explicitly exempted from Bearer token auth in api-server.ts setupAuth hook — they handle their own user-level JWT auth.")
PlatformApi.description: Layer 2 platform routes: chat/message doorman routing, bridge queue, capabilities, resources, cloud instances, content registry, auth (guest/claim/login), projects CRUD, deploy/undeploy, hosting, and app serving.

_tags: @gotcha("Session-aware: tries loadSession() first for encrypted identities. If session.json exists, the node starts with that identity without prompting for password.")
@gotcha("Port pre-check: if API port is occupied, CLI attempts to shut down the existing instance via POST /admin/shutdown before failing.")
@gotcha("RESTART_EXIT_CODE = 75 — PM2/systemd/start-node.bat restarts the process when it exits with this code.")
@gotcha("MSYS2 path normalization: /c/Users/... is converted to C:\\Users\\... on Windows because path.join mishandles MSYS2 paths.")
@why("DEFAULT_BOOTSTRAPS contains 3 nodes (LS-1, EC2-1, EC2-2) for mesh connectivity — ensures new nodes connect to at least 2 bootstrap peers.")
@why("Public IP auto-detection uses AWS IMDS v1 (http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/public-ipv4) with 2s timeout — works on EC2 and Lightsail, silently skips elsewhere.")
CliEntryPoint.description: Non-interactive CLI entry point: parses flags, initializes PandoNode with MongoDB/storage backend, sets up file logging, crash guard, port pre-check, post-deploy health checks, and heartbeat reporting.

PORT_PRECHECK.what: Node failed to start because previous instance still held the API port
PORT_PRECHECK.why: PM2 restart or crash left the old process running, and Fastify's listen() fails immediately on EADDRINUSE
PORT_PRECHECK.fix: Added port pre-check that attempts graceful shutdown of existing instance via /admin/shutdown API, waits up to 15s for port release

_tags: @gotcha("listenPort 0 means the OS picks a random available port — the actual port is only known after libp2p starts listening.")
NodeConfig.description: Default NodeConfig factory and port parsing utility — provides sensible defaults (port 0 = random, apiPort 4000, dataDir ~/.pando, mode full).

_tags: @gotcha("Bridge Watcher is event-driven (newItem/managerIdle), not timer-based — no heartbeats.")
@gotcha("Failed events retry up to 3 times, then escalate to parent agent or log if top-level.")
@gotcha("Stale processing detection at 2.5 hours — covers case where crash left manager in 'busy' state.")
@why("Per-manager queues in BridgeQueue, not a single global queue — prevents one slow project from blocking another.")
@why("Agent registry uses in-memory Map + disk persistence (index.json) for fast lookup with crash recovery.")
AgentManager.description: Agent lifecycle manager — owns BridgeQueue, routes events to agents, manages spawn/resume/rotate/archive, creates pando-node-mgr on startup.

AGENT_SERIALIZATION.rule: Only one event processed per manager at a time — BridgeQueue.setManagerBusy gates concurrent access

_tags: @gotcha("stdin MUST be 'ignore', not 'pipe' — Claude Code buffers all stdin until EOF, causing hangs.")
@gotcha("CLAUDECODE env var MUST be deleted before spawning to prevent 'nested session' errors.")
@gotcha("CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY and PANDO_STORAGE_URL are stripped from child env — agents must never access credentials directly.")
@gotcha("Agent workspaces at ~/.pando/agents/<id>/workspace/ are EPHEMERAL — results go to StorageBackend, workspaces are auto-cleaned after completion.")
@gotcha("Events are serialized per-agent: one Claude Code spawn at a time, extras queued in eventQueue array.")
@why("Per-event spawn model (claude -p --continue --resume <sid>) instead of long-running process — avoids zombie processes, allows state persistence between spawns.")
@why("4-layer CLAUDE.md template (role, project state, learned lessons, task context) gives agents scoped context without overwhelming token limits.")
Agent.description: Universal agent primitive — every agent (manager, builder, tester, reviewer, researcher, devops) is the same class with different templates.

AGENT_STDIN_PIPE_HANG.what: Agents hung indefinitely when stdin was set to 'pipe'
AGENT_STDIN_PIPE_HANG.why: Claude Code reads all of stdin before starting — pipe keeps it waiting forever
AGENT_STDIN_PIPE_HANG.fix: Changed stdin to 'ignore' in spawn options

AGENT_NESTED_SESSION.what: Claude Code errored with 'nested session' when spawned from within Claude Code
AGENT_NESTED_SESSION.why: CLAUDECODE env var leaked from parent process to child
AGENT_NESTED_SESSION.fix: Delete env.CLAUDECODE before spawning child process

AGENT_CREDENTIAL_LEAK.what: Agent child processes had access to CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY and PANDO_STORAGE_URL
AGENT_CREDENTIAL_LEAK.why: Environment variables inherited from parent process by default
AGENT_CREDENTIAL_LEAK.fix: Explicitly delete CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY and PANDO_STORAGE_URL from child env

AGENT_HARD_LIMITS.rule: Max depth 5, max 50 agents per project, budget limit enforced in code (not just templates)

_tags: @gotcha("stdin is 'ignore' — never 'pipe'. Claude Code buffers all stdin until EOF.")
@gotcha("CLAUDECODE, CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY, and PANDO_STORAGE_URL are deleted from child env.")
@gotcha("Uses --dangerously-skip-permissions flag — agents run without permission prompts.")
@why("Per-event spawn with 'claude -p --continue --resume <sessionId>' maintains conversation context without long-running processes.")
@why("stream-json output format parsed line-by-line to extract text blocks, tool usage, session ID, and cost from structured events.")
ClaudeBackend.description: Claude Code AI backend — spawns claude CLI with per-event model, parses stream-json output, enforces idle/hard-cap timeouts.

CLAUDE_RESUME_SESSION.what: First spawn captures sessionId, subsequent spawns use --continue --resume for continuity
CLAUDE_RESUME_SESSION.why: Claude Code sessions are stateful — resume preserves conversation history
CLAUDE_RESUME_SESSION.fix: Parse 'system' event type for session_id, store it, pass to future spawns

_tags: @gotcha("detect() returns true if Ollama is running, but execute() always returns an error — not functional yet.")
OllamaBackend.description: Ollama AI backend stub — detects localhost:11434 availability but execute() is not yet implemented.

_tags: @gotcha("getBest() returns the FIRST available backend matching the capability — order of registration matters.")
@why("detectAll() runs in parallel for speed — all backends probe concurrently at startup.")
AIBackendRegistry.description: Runtime registry that detects, manages, and selects the best available AI backend for a given task type.

_tags: @why("Agents must never spawn 'claude' directly — all AI execution goes through AIBackendRegistry.getBest(taskType) for backend portability.")
AIBackend.description: Interface for pluggable AI execution backends — abstracts agent system from any specific AI provider.

_tags: @gotcha("Queues are per-manager (Map<managerId, BridgeItem[]>), NOT a single global queue — multiple projects do NOT share a queue.")
@gotcha("urgency:direct items bypass the Manager queue entirely and go straight to user via SSE — max 1 direct bypass per taskId.")
@gotcha("Items within the same priority tier are sorted FIFO by timestamp; priority tiers sort by PRIORITY_ORDER.")
@why("Event-driven, not timer-based: 'newItem' triggers immediate processing, 'managerIdle' triggers next-item check — zero heartbeats.")
BridgeQueue.description: Event-driven per-manager FIFO communication hub — priority-ordered (CRITICAL > NORMAL > LOW), emits newItem/managerIdle for Bridge Watcher pattern.

BRIDGE_PER_PROJECT.what: FIFO is per-project (per-manager). Multiple projects do NOT share a queue.
BRIDGE_PER_PROJECT.why: Each manager has its own queue keyed by managerId to prevent cross-project blocking
BRIDGE_PER_PROJECT.fix: Design decision from Phase 27 — always key queues by managerId

_tags: @gotcha("AWS SDK is imported dynamically — only loaded when launchInstance/terminateInstance is called.")
@gotcha("Security group intentionally has NO port 22 (SSH). Instances are managed entirely via P2P.")
@gotcha("Auto-links instances to P2P peers by matching IP addresses when peers connect (10s delay for settlement).")
@gotcha("Tripwire monitor script runs as root, checks every 1s for: logins, sshd, SSM agent, debugger, interactive root. Any detection = wipe + shutdown.")
@gotcha("AWS credentials are wiped from local scope after each API call (set to empty string) for security.")
@why("User-data bootstrap removes SSH+SSM FIRST before installing anything else — security before functionality.")
@why("Instance records persisted to SQLite (cloud_instances table) so tracking survives node restarts.")
CloudInstanceManager.description: Launches and manages secure EC2 compute instances — no SSH, tripwire monitoring, all management via P2P request-reply.

_tags: @gotcha("Only nodes with CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY env var can encrypt/decrypt — user nodes get null from getCredential().")
@gotcha("wipe() zeros out the master key in memory and cannot be recovered without process restart — used by tripwire on security compromise.")
@gotcha("getActiveByType() iterates all active credentials of a type and tries each — skips expired and failed decryptions.")
@why("Two-tier trust model: EC2 compute nodes (trusted, have master key) vs user nodes (untrusted, route via P2P credential-op proxy).")
@why("Collection name 'pando_credentials' is blocklisted in P2PStorageBackend handler — credentials never proxy through P2P storage.")
CredentialStore.description: MongoDB-based encrypted credential storage — AES-256-GCM with CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY, only usable by trusted compute nodes.

_tags: @gotcha("Ciphertext format is encrypted data + 16-byte auth tag concatenated, then base64 encoded. Nonce is separate base64 field.")
@why("X25519 ECDH key wrapping was removed in Phase 69 — single master key model replaced per-node key wrapping for simplicity.")
CredentialVault.description: AES-256-GCM encryption utilities — encryptCredential() and decryptCredential() with random 12-byte nonce per credential.

_tags: @gotcha("Only one active backup at a time — creating a new backup removes the previous one.")
@gotcha("rollbackCommit() uses git revert if HEAD has moved past the target, or git reset --soft if HEAD matches.")
@gotcha("Build timeout is 3 minutes (180s). Push defaults to origin/master.")
@why("Commits only the specific files listed in the PatchSet, not git add -A, to avoid committing unintended changes.")
DeployManager.description: Git commit, build, and rollback pipeline for autonomous code changes — manages backup/restore of the packages/ directory.

_tags: @gotcha("Import boundary rule: core/* may import kernel/*, @pando/shared, @pando/ledger, and npm packages — NEVER from platform/*.")
CoreBarrel.description: Barrel export for Core layer (Layer 1) — re-exports agent system, storage, credentials, deploy, payment, cloud, and P2P request-reply.

CORE_IMPORT_BOUNDARY.rule: core/ modules must never import from platform/ — only kernel/, @pando/shared, @pando/ledger, and npm packages

_tags: @gotcha("MongoDB driver is imported dynamically to avoid hard dependency — only loaded when this backend is actually used.")
@gotcha("_id and id fields are stripped from data on putRecord to avoid immutable-field conflicts; getRecord/queryRecords rename _id back to id.")
@gotcha("getDb() exposes raw MongoDB Db instance for CredentialStore — only available on compute nodes with PANDO_STORAGE_URL.")
@why("Collections map 1:1: putRecord('threads', id, data) maps to db.collection('threads').updateOne({_id: id}, {$set: data}, {upsert: true}).")
MongoStorageBackend.description: MongoDB implementation of StorageBackend — stores user data (threads, messages, projects, user accounts) with collection-level indexes.

_tags: @gotcha("Startup grace period: waits up to 30s for compute peers to connect before failing, polling every 1s.")
@gotcha("Sticky peer affinity: successful requests set preferredPeerId, failures clear it to try a different peer.")
@gotcha("Max 3 attempts per operation — tries preferred peer first, then cycles through others.")
@gotcha("Does NOT expose getDb() — CredentialStore only initializes on compute nodes, never via P2P proxy.")
@why("Collection blocklist (pando_credentials) and method allowlist (6 CRUD methods) enforced at handler level on compute node, not here.")
P2PStorageBackend.description: Storage proxy for untrusted nodes — forwards all CRUD operations via P2P request-reply to compute nodes with MongoDB.

P2P_STORAGE_FAILOVER.what: P2P storage automatically fails over to next mongodb node if primary is down
P2P_STORAGE_FAILOVER.why: preferredPeerId is cleared on failure, next attempt tries a different compute peer
P2P_STORAGE_FAILOVER.fix: orderPeers() puts preferred first, but failure clears affinity and MAX_ATTEMPTS cycles through available peers

_tags: @gotcha("Payment holds expire after 24 hours — stale holds are lazily cleaned on next holdPayment() or getPaymentHistory() call.")
@gotcha("Free tier categories (search, ledger, network, system) and trivial complexity always cost 0 Lux.")
@gotcha("Uses LedgerLike minimal interface, not full PandoLedger — keeps module decoupled.")
@gotcha("History trimmed to last 1000 records, completed holds older than 7 days cleaned up.")
@why("Escrow goes to NETWORK account during hold, then transferred to recipient on release — prevents double-spending.")
@why("Cost breakdown: compute 70%, storage 10%, network 20% of base cost by complexity tier.")
PaymentGate.description: Lux payment escrow and cost estimation — holds funds during task execution, releases to executor on completion, refunds on failure.

_tags: @gotcha("Phase 93: Direct TCP tried first for unicast, falls back to GossipSub — makes P2P storage proxy reliable without mesh formation.")
@gotcha("Rate limits: 120 requests/min, 240 replies/min (sliding window). Increased in Phase 83 for storage proxy traffic.")
@gotcha("Broadcast queries (to: '*') always use GossipSub — direct TCP is only for targeted peer requests.")
@gotcha("Reply also tries direct TCP first, then GossipSub — both directions use the same fallback pattern.")
@why("Separate pending maps for single requests vs broadcast queries — single requests resolve on first reply, queries collect up to maxReplies within timeout.")
RequestReplyManager.description: Request/reply messaging over direct TCP streams with GossipSub fallback — correlation IDs, timeouts, rate limiting, latency tracking.

_tags: @why("Nodes are stateless compute proxies — user data lives on internet infrastructure (MongoDB), not on nodes. StorageBackend abstracts the storage location.")
@why("Two implementations: MongoStorageBackend (direct, for compute nodes) and P2PStorageBackend (proxy via P2P, for untrusted nodes).")
StorageBackend.description: Pluggable storage interface for user data — 6 CRUD methods (putRecord, getRecord, queryRecords, deleteRecord, listRecords, pushToArray) plus init/close.

_tags: @gotcha("Hash verification is soft — orphan branch pushes produce different hashes, so mismatch logs a warning but proceeds.")
@gotcha("Build failure triggers automatic rollback to previous commit via git reset --hard.")
@gotcha("Version pinning (pinVersion/unpinVersion) blocks all upgrades until unpinned.")
@gotcha("Restart uses exit code 75 — process supervisor (PM2/systemd) must be configured to restart on this code.")
@why("Catch-up timer (5 min interval, 30s startup delay) independently scans governance for missed upgrades — no dependency on the proposing node staying online.")
@why("createUpgradeProposal() fetches origin/master first to propose remote HEAD, not local HEAD — ensures peers actually pull new code.")
UpgradeProtocol.description: Self-upgrade via governance-approved git pull + hash verification + build + restart — broadcasts upgrade notifications to all peers via GossipSub.

UPGRADE_GIT_OWNERSHIP.what: git repo owned by pando user, npm ci runs as root during bootstrap — chown needed
UPGRADE_GIT_OWNERSHIP.why: Bootstrap runs as root, but node process runs as pando user — file ownership mismatch
UPGRADE_GIT_OWNERSHIP.fix: Bootstrap script does chown -R pando:pando /opt/pando after npm ci

UPGRADE_GIT_IDENTITY.what: pando user needs git user.name + user.email set, otherwise git commit fails
UPGRADE_GIT_IDENTITY.why: git commit requires author identity — pando system user has no default git config
UPGRADE_GIT_IDENTITY.fix: Bootstrap script sets git config --global user.name/user.email for pando user

_tags: @gotcha("Major version mismatch is always incompatible — no cross-major communication.")
@gotcha("canClaimTask() checks both minimum version AND required feature capabilities.")
@why("Default capabilities (messaging, ledger-sync, governance, task-sync, code-pipeline) are advertised by every node — feature gates are per-capability, not per-version.")
VersionProtocol.description: Multi-node version coordination — semver compatibility checks, task eligibility by version/capabilities, upgrade detection.

_tags: @gotcha("PandoNode is a GOD OBJECT with 50+ private fields — each subsystem is nullable and initialized conditionally during start(). Always null-check before use.")
@gotcha("detectClaudeCode() has a 3-second timeout — on slow systems (Windows especially) this can delay startup.")
@gotcha("Daily emission cap (500 Lux) is tracked in-memory (dailyEmissions) and reset by date string comparison — restarting the node resets the counter.")

@gotcha("Peer exchange runs at 5s after each peer connect, plus 30s and 90s after boot. It shares addresses from getConnectedPeerAddresses() which includes peerStore announce addresses for NAT/VPC traversal.")
@gotcha("Governance re-sync runs every 5 min to catch missed votes/decisions in thin GossipSub meshes (<6 peers).")
@why("Subsystems are initialized in layered order: kernel (network, ledger, sync) -> core (agents, storage) -> platform (scheduler, resources). This matches the import boundary rule.")
PandoNode.description: Main PandoNode class that wires together all subsystems (kernel, core, platform layers), manages startup/shutdown lifecycle, and exposes getters for every subsystem.

_tags: @gotcha("Double-rollback protection: if a rollback already happened within 2x the crash window (120s), CrashGuard refuses to rollback again and waits for manual intervention.")
@gotcha("Stability delay is 30 seconds — markStable() must be called after this period to clear the crash log. If the node crashes before 30s, the startup is counted toward crash loop detection.")
@gotcha("restoreDistBackups copies dist.backup/ to dist/ for all 5 packages (shared, ledger, node, gateway, mcp-server). Only packages with existing dist.backup/ are restored.")

@why("Crash log is stored at ~/.pando/crash-log.json — simple JSON with timestamp array. Launcher scripts (start-node.bat / start-node.command) auto-restart the node, so CrashGuard only needs to restore a working build.")
CrashGuard.description: Binary rollback safety net — tracks node startup timestamps, detects crash loops (3+ crashes in 60s), and restores dist/ from dist.backup/ to recover a working build.

_tags: @gotcha("Rate limited to 10 proposals per node per hour. Rate limits are persisted to ~/.pando/emission-rates.json.")
@gotcha("Only the PROPOSING node actually mints Lux — other nodes just witness and attest. This prevents double-minting.")
@gotcha("Bootstrap fallback: if peerCount < 3 (BOOTSTRAP_NODE_THRESHOLD), proposals auto-approve immediately without witnesses. This is critical for single-node or tiny network bootstrapping.")
@gotcha("A witness can NEVER attest their own proposal — proposal.peerId must differ from attestation.witnessPeerId.")
@why("Proposals expire after 5 minutes to prevent stale emissions from being finalized late.")
@why("Anti-replay uses processedAttestations Set keyed by 'witnessPeerId:proposalId' — cleared when size exceeds 10000.")
EmissionWitness.description: Witness-based Lux emission system — nodes propose emissions, peers validate and sign WitnessAttestations (Ed25519), and quorum of 2+ independent witnesses finalizes the mint. Bootstrap fallback for networks with <3 nodes.

EMISSION_QUORUM.rule: Emissions require 2+ independent witness attestations before Lux is minted (except bootstrap fallback for <3 node networks)

_tags: @gotcha("Proposals require a 10 Lux stake (PROPOSAL_STAKE_LUX). Emergency proposals cost 50 Lux. Nodes with balance < 100 Lux get their first proposal free (FREE_TIER_THRESHOLD).")
@gotcha("Governance-change proposals (category 'governance_change') have stricter rules: 24h voting period, 80% approval threshold, minimum 5 votes. This is meta-governance protection (Phase 30.6).")
@gotcha("Upgrade proposals auto-approve when vote count reaches upgradeAutoApproveThreshold (default 8). This enables P2P self-upgrade without waiting for voting period to expire.")
@gotcha("All proposals, votes, and decisions are persisted to SQLite (ledger.db) AND held in-memory caches (Maps). On start, both are loaded from DB. Max 500 proposals in memory before eviction.")
@gotcha("User input is sanitized via sanitizeText() to prevent stored XSS — angle brackets are HTML-entity encoded.")

@why("Reviewer candidacy uses a 5-minute window (CANDIDACY_WINDOW_MS) so multiple nodes can volunteer. Reviewers are selected by reputation score, with fallback attempts if the primary reviewer fails (max 2 fallback attempts).")
@why("Model attestation signs SHA-256 hash with Ed25519 to cryptographically prove which AI model cast a vote — prevents spoofed AI votes.")
GovernanceSync.description: Decentralized governance system — proposals, discussion, voting, and consensus via GossipSub. Supports AI-powered reviews (Phase 30), reputation-weighted voting (Phase 12.4), proposal staking, reviewer selection, upgrade auto-approve, and meta-governance protection.

GOVERNANCE_PROPOSAL_STAKE.what: New node identities with < 10 Lux cannot create governance proposals
GOVERNANCE_PROPOSAL_STAKE.why: Proposals require staking 10 Lux as anti-spam measure. New nodes start with low balance from genesis allocation.
GOVERNANCE_PROPOSAL_STAKE.fix: Transfer Lux from another node first, or wait for uptime emissions to accumulate >= 10 Lux

GOVERNANCE_META_PROTECTION.rule: Proposals in category 'governance_change' require 80% approval, 24h voting, and minimum 5 votes — stricter than standard proposals

_tags: @gotcha("IMMUTABLE_KERNEL_FILES can NEVER be modified by the autonomous pipeline — any attempt is auto-rejected. These include crypto.ts, guardrails.ts, governance.ts, transactions.ts, code-pipeline.ts, deploy-manager.ts, identity.ts.")
@gotcha("Governance-approved changes bypass protected path checks AND rate limits — voting IS the approval mechanism.")
@gotcha("postCheck runs npm build with 2min timeout and npm test with 5min timeout. Error messages are sanitized to strip absolute paths.")
@gotcha("tieredPreCheck is ADDITIVE to the base preCheck — both systems coexist.")

@why("Tiered guardrails exist because different files have different risk levels. Critical files (network, sync, ledger, crypto) need approval + review + test + build. Low-risk files only need build.")
@why("Config stored at ~/.pando/guardrails.json and pending changes at ~/.pando/guardrails-pending.json — both created with defaults on first run.")
Guardrails.description: Safety system for self-generated code changes — enforces protected paths, rate limits (hourly/daily), tiered guardrail checks (Critical/Important/Standard/Low), immutable kernel file protection, and pending-change approval queue.

GUARDRAILS_CANNOT_DISABLE.rule: Guardrails themselves are in the immutable kernel list — agents cannot modify guardrails.ts to weaken safety checks

_tags: @gotcha("LocalEnvironment is NOT exported from kernel/index.ts despite being in the kernel/ directory — it may be imported directly when needed.")
KernelIndex.description: Barrel export file for Layer 0 (Kernel) — re-exports all kernel modules: PandoNetwork, LedgerSync, GovernanceSync, HealthMonitor, Guardrails, SecurityMonitor, ReputationManager, EmissionWitness, NetworkState, CrashGuard, RestartReason.

KERNEL_IMPORT_BOUNDARY.rule: kernel/ modules may only import from kernel/*, @pando/shared, @pando/ledger, and external npm packages — NEVER from core/ or platform/

_tags: @gotcha("PRIVACY INVARIANT: Everything in LocalEnvironment is Envelope 1 — NEVER synced via P2P GossipSub, NEVER uploaded to MongoDB or S3, NEVER accessible from outside this machine.")
@gotcha("Protected paths (.pando/identities, .pando/session.json, .ssh, .gnupg, .aws/credentials) are ALWAYS blocked from reading — even in granted directories.")
@gotcha("Agents access local files via HTTP API only — never direct filesystem. Index lives in Envelope 1.")
@gotcha("Files > 512KB are skipped during indexing. Only known code/text extensions are indexed (INDEXABLE_EXTENSIONS set).")
@why("Uses SQLite FTS5 virtual table for full-text search — separate from the ledger database. Stored at ~/.pando/file-index.db.")
LocalEnvironment.description: Envelope 1 local file indexing and user memory — grants directories for FTS5 full-text search over local files, manages user memory entries, with strict privacy guarantees (never synced via P2P, never uploaded).

ENVELOPE_1_PRIVACY.rule: LocalEnvironment data must NEVER leave the local machine — no P2P sync, no cloud upload, no external access

_tags: @gotcha("This is DATA-ONLY — it NEVER takes recovery actions or restarts anything. The manager agent decides what to act on based on alerts.")

@gotcha("Alert dedup uses a 3-case upsert: (1) active alert → increment count, (2) recently-resolved alert within 30min → reopen, (3) otherwise → new entry. Prevents oscillating conditions from flooding alerts.")
@gotcha("Recovery config is persisted to ~/.pando/monitor/recovery-config.json — loads with backward compat from legacy recovery.json.")
@why("Event loop lag measurement uses setInterval with unref() so it does not prevent Node.js from exiting gracefully.")
@why("Separate external references via setters (setSchedulerProvider, setNetworkProvider) to avoid circular imports between kernel modules.")
HealthMonitor.description: DATA-ONLY health monitoring — collects rolling metrics, detects 8 alert types (scheduler down, no peers, high failure rate, consecutive failures, high memory, event loop lag, ledger sync lag, agent spawn failures), and persists state to ~/.pando/monitor/.

MONITOR_NO_RECOVERY.rule: HealthMonitor must NEVER take autonomous recovery actions — it only collects data and generates alerts

_tags: @gotcha("Uses PandoNode typed as 'any' to avoid circular imports — accesses subsystems via getNetwork(), getLedger(), getMonitor() etc. All collectors are wrapped in try/catch to degrade gracefully.")
@gotcha("Hourly auto-generation timer uses unref() so it does not prevent Node.js from exiting.")
@why("Written as markdown (not JSON) because the primary consumer is AI council reflection sessions that read natural language better than structured data.")
NetworkState.description: Periodically aggregates metrics from all subsystems (network, economy, resources, tasks, health, governance) into a NetworkStateSnapshot and writes it as markdown to ~/.pando/council/network-state.md for council reflection sessions.

_tags: @gotcha("GossipSub topic subscriptions are deduplicated — subscribing twice to the same topic is a no-op. All topic listeners are cleaned up in stop() to prevent leaks on restart.")
@gotcha("Known peers are persisted to ~/.pando/known-peers.json with 7-day TTL and 50-peer cap. On startup, known peers are re-dialed automatically.")
@gotcha("Peer exchange includes peerStore announce addresses (public IPs from identify protocol), not just connection addresses. This is critical for NAT/VPC traversal.")
@gotcha("Agent message payload limit is 256KB (increased from 8KB) to support P2P storage proxy responses containing large project/thread data.")
@why("announce addresses are configured via PUBLIC_IP env var on cloud nodes — required because 0.0.0.0 bind address is not externally reachable behind NAT/VPC.")
@why("updateKnownPeer is delayed 3s after connect to allow the identify protocol to populate peerStore with announce addresses.")
