PandoNetwork.description: Core P2P networking layer built on libp2p with TCP+Noise encryption, Yamux muxing, mDNS/bootstrap discovery, GossipSub pub/sub, and circuit relay support.

IPV6_GATEWAY_FAILURE.why: Node.js may resolve localhost to ::1 (IPv6) which libp2p/Fastify may not bind
IPV6_GATEWAY_FAILURE.fix: Always use 127.0.0.1 instead of localhost for local connections

ED25519_PUBKEY_FROM_PEERID.what: Cross-node auth failed because ledger stored 'remote-peer' as public key
ED25519_PUBKEY_FROM_PEERID.why: Remote nodes registered with placeholder public key, making signature verification impossible
ED25519_PUBKEY_FROM_PEERID.fix: Extract public key from peerId string via peerIdFromString().publicKey — no ledger lookup needed

VPC_INTERNAL_IP_LEAK.what: Peer exchange shared internal VPC IPs (172.31.x.x) that external nodes could not dial
VPC_INTERNAL_IP_LEAK.why: EC2 nodes in the same VPC connect via internal IPs. connection.remoteAddr returns the internal IP, not the public announce address.
VPC_INTERNAL_IP_LEAK.fix: getConnectedPeerAddresses() and updateKnownPeer() now also query libp2p peerStore for announce addresses (public IPs from identify protocol). AWS IMDS auto-detects public IP on cloud nodes.

GOSSIPSUB_DEDUP.rule: Each GossipSub topic must only be subscribed once per PandoNetwork instance — subscribedTopics Set enforces this

_tags: @gotcha("Remote reputation scores are RECOMPUTED from claimed stats — self-reported scores are never trusted. Anti-spoofing: nodeId must match sender peerId.")
@gotcha("Only broadcasts when score changes by >5% (BROADCAST_THRESHOLD) to prevent spam. First non-zero score always broadcasts.")
@gotcha("Peer records are pruned every 6 hours: stale records (>7 days) removed, then enforces 1000-record cap by removing oldest.")
@why("Score formula: (completed*2) + (buildPassRate*10) + (testPassRate*10) - (failed*3) - (timedOut*5) + (profiles*1) — weighted to reward reliability over volume.")
@why("History stripped from broadcast payloads to save bandwidth — only stats fields are sent over P2P.")
ReputationManager.description: Tracks node performance reputation across the network — scores based on tasks completed, build/test pass rates, completion speed, and peer endorsements; syncs via GossipSub agent-events and RequestReplyManager.

_tags: @gotcha("File is cleaned up after successful health check via clearRestartReason() — if not cleared, the next startup will incorrectly assume a deploy restart.")
@why("Stored as ~/.pando/restart-reason.json — simple JSON with reason and timestamp. Separate from crash-guard because these are intentional restarts, not crashes.")
RestartReason.description: Simple restart-reason file writer/reader — records why a restart was triggered (auto-update or pipeline-deploy) so cli.ts can run post-deploy health checks on startup.

_tags: @gotcha("Critical alerts auto-quarantine the offending peer. Quarantine auto-expires after 1 hour. Three quarantine levels: L1 (stop messages), L2 (broadcast notice), L3 (emergency governance vote).")
@gotcha("Alerts and quarantine entries are persisted to ~/.pando/security/alerts.json and quarantine.json. Max 200 entries each.")
@gotcha("A node can NEVER quarantine itself — all quarantine methods check peerId !== localPeerId.")
@why("Detectors implement the AnomalyDetector interface with a check() method — runs every 30 seconds. Each detector maintains its own sliding window of events.")
SecurityMonitor.description: Threat detection and peer quarantine system with 5 specialized detectors: MessageRateMonitor (GossipSub flooding), TransactionConflictDetector (double-spend), SybilDetector (correlated peer clusters), ProfilePoisoningDetector (XSS/injection), EmissionAbuseDetector (emission spam).

_tags: @gotcha("Dedup uses two Sets (processedTxs + appliedTxs) as belt-and-suspenders against async race conditions where two identical txs pass the sync check simultaneously.")
@gotcha("Sync request includes local txCount so responders can detect large gaps and send full history instead of just recent window.")
@gotcha("Unsigned transfers are REJECTED — only emissions (signed by NETWORK) are allowed without real signatures.")
@gotcha("Periodic sync check runs every 60s to close transaction gaps. On peer connect, sync is requested at 5s AND retried at 30s to handle GossipSub mesh forming delay.")
@why("processedTxs and appliedTxs are periodically pruned (cleanup method) to prevent unbounded memory growth — keeps last 5000 of each.")
@why("Account claims carry balance so receiving nodes can create accounts with correct balance and keep totalSupply consistent (fixes welcome-bonus divergence bug).")
LedgerSync.description: Distributed ledger synchronization via GossipSub — broadcasts transactions in real-time, catches up missed transactions on peer connect, and syncs account claims and activity records.

TX_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED.rule: All TRANSFER type transactions must have a valid Ed25519 signature — unsigned transfers are rejected

_tags: @gotcha("Rotation is checked AFTER every write — a single huge log line could temporarily exceed 5MB before rotation kicks in.")
@gotcha("If the log file cannot be opened (permissions, disk full), FileLogger silently skips all writes rather than crashing the node.")
@why("ANSI stripping ensures log files are readable via SSH/cat without terminal escape code garbage.")
FileLogger.description: Writes timestamped, ANSI-stripped log lines to ~/.pando/logs/node.log with automatic rotation at 5MB (one .log.1 backup).

_tags: @gotcha("Auth is NOT checked per-route -- the global onRequest hook in api-server.ts enforces Bearer token auth on all POST/PUT/DELETE routes.")
@why("Separating agent routes from api-server.ts keeps the route file focused and allows independent testing.")
AgentTools.description: HTTP API endpoints for agent lifecycle (spawn, message, report, tree, connect, status, reset-session). Agents call these via curl from Claude Code sessions. Auth enforced by global Fastify hook.

_tags: @gotcha("Node.js capability is always present (hardcoded). Claude Code detection checks for the 'claude' binary and valid auth credentials file.")
@why("Auto-detection eliminates manual capability configuration. Nodes advertise what they actually have, not what an operator claims.")
CapabilityDetector.description: Auto-detects node capabilities at startup: claude-code CLI, Docker daemon, Python 3, Node.js (always), NVIDIA GPU, Playwright. Supports manual overrides from config. Detection results feed into CapabilityRegistry.

_tags: @gotcha("Profiles expire after 15 minutes of no refresh. If a peer stops broadcasting, it silently disappears from the registry.")
@why("TTL-based expiry ensures the capability map reflects the live network. Dead nodes are automatically pruned without explicit removal.")
CapabilityRegistry.description: Network-wide capability map. Stores CapabilityProfiles from peers via GossipSub with 15-minute TTL. Queryable by capability type. Used by Scheduler, ResourceRouter, and deploy system to find capable nodes.

capability_registry_public_ip.what: Tier 2 deploys routed to wrong IP because CapabilityProfile contained only internal/P2P addresses
capability_registry_public_ip.why: EC2 nodes behind VPC NAT advertise 0.0.0.0 or internal IPs, not their public IP
capability_registry_public_ip.fix: publicAddress field on CapabilityProfile must be set via PUBLIC_IP env var on EC2

_tags: @gotcha("extractDiff() first tries to parse structured output files. If that fails, extractGitDiff() falls back to running git diff in the workspace. Both produce the same PatchSet format.")
@why("Guardrail pre-check before patch application prevents agents from modifying immutable kernel files or violating tiered access rules.")
CodePipeline.description: Extracts diffs from agent workspace output directories, applies patches through guardrail checks (immutable kernel + tiered pre-check), supports full file-by-file rollback. Has extractDiff() with extractGitDiff() fallback.

kernel_immutability.rule: Patches targeting files in kernel/ are rejected by Guardrails.preCheck(). Agents cannot modify Layer 0 code.

_tags: @gotcha("Task creation is via a callback (setTaskCreator) -- if no callback is set, issues are detected but no tasks are created.")
@why("Auto-maintenance ensures deployed content stays healthy without manual monitoring. Task creation via callback avoids circular dependency with TaskQueue.")
ContentMaintenance.description: Periodic health scanner for owned content. Detects unhealthy, stale, or down content and creates maintenance tasks via task queue callback. Runs on 1-hour scan interval with 10-second health check timeout.

_tags: @gotcha("extractContent() walks the workspace directory recursively but skips node_modules, .git, and other standard ignore patterns.")
@why("Publishing is separated from the registry so that workspace extraction logic does not pollute the P2P sync layer.")
ContentPublisher.description: Handles the publish flow for agent-built content. Extracts output from workspace directories, creates ContentRecords with SHA-256 content hashes, and announces to the network via ContentRegistry.

_tags: @gotcha("Remote records from GossipSub are merged via mergeRemoteRecord() which skips records from localPeerId to prevent echo loops.")
@why("Content layer makes agent-built artifacts discoverable across the entire network without a central index.")
ContentRegistry.description: SQLite-backed content record registry with GossipSub sync on pando/content topic. Records websites, APIs, datasets, services, documents, tools built by agents. Provides full-text search on title + description + tags.

_tags: @gotcha("No AI or external API calls -- purely regex pattern matching. This means it catches known patterns but cannot detect novel threats.")
@why("Law I compliance. Content must be checked before publishing to prevent harmful material from propagating across the network.")
ContentSafetyReviewer.description: Rule-based content safety reviewer (Phase 12.5). Checks for harmful content, malicious code, dependency vulnerabilities, OWASP patterns, and Two Laws compliance. Entirely rule-based pattern matching -- no external API calls. Reviews persisted at ~/.pando/security/safety-reviews.json.

two_laws_safety.rule: Content targeting humans with violence or self-harm instructions must always be flagged as critical severity.

_tags: @gotcha("Scores use 10% monthly exponential decay: weight * 0.9^monthsSince. This means old contributions lose value over time -- recent work counts more.")
@why("Time-decayed scoring prevents early contributors from dominating revenue shares forever. Active contributors are rewarded more than passive historical ones.")
ContributionTracker.description: MongoDB-first contribution tracking (Phase 31.9, 57). Records individual contributions (code/review/test/design/management/documentation), verifies via admin, calculates time-decayed scores (10% monthly decay), derives proportional revenue shares.

_tags: @gotcha("Council members are selected based on CapabilityProfile details (claudeCode: true), NOT just NodeCapability.CLAUDE_CODE enum. The AI call in runDailyReflection() is STUBBED -- infrastructure only.")
@why("Self-governance brain of the network. The council pattern ensures decisions come from high-reputation, AI-capable nodes rather than random peers.")
Council.description: Network Council selection and reflection engine (Phase 50). Rotating top-3 AI-capable nodes by reputation. Weekly rotation, daily/weekly/monthly reflection cycles. Assembles prompts from network state, council minutes, and genome state.

council_ai_stubbed.what: runDailyReflection() AI call is STUBBED — council does not actually call Claude yet
council_ai_stubbed.why: AI backend integration was deferred; infrastructure (prompt assembly, minutes, rotation) was built first
council_ai_stubbed.fix: Assembles prompt and writes to last-prompt.md, returns placeholder summary until AI backend is wired

_tags: @gotcha("Purely in-memory -- claims are lost on restart. clearAll() is called on startup to prevent stale locks from persisting after a crash.")
@why("Local-only design avoids P2P consensus overhead for file locking. Since agents run on the same node, local coordination is sufficient.")
FileRegistry.description: Local-only file ownership registry preventing concurrent edits by multiple agents. In-memory Map with 15-minute TTL auto-expiry. Claims are per-peerId, auto-pruned on every operation. No P2P sync.

_tags: @gotcha("Parses genome.yaml manually (line-by-line, no YAML library). Maps code files to genome components via frontmatter 'entry' field in component markdown files. Keyword matching is used when direct file mapping fails.")
@why("The genome is the single source of truth for architecture. Keeping it accurate automatically via git commit watching eliminates manual documentation burden.")
GenomeAgent.description: Self-maintaining Project Genome agent (Phase 25). Watches git commits, maps code changes to genome components, detects drift (missing files, broken deps), generates scoped context for worker agents via getScopedContext().

_tags: @gotcha("AWS credentials are picked up from ~/.aws/credentials automatically -- no explicit credential config. If missing, all S3 operations fail silently.")
@why("S3 hosting is the Tier 1 deployment target. Cheap, globally distributed, no server management. Tier 2 (PM2+nginx on EC2) is for dynamic apps.")
HostingService.description: S3-based project hosting (Phase 32). Public projects served via S3 static website endpoint. Private/shared projects use pre-signed URLs with 1-hour TTL. Bucket layout: public/<projectId>/ (readable) vs private/<projectId>/ (signed).

_tags: @why("Barrel file provides a single import point for all platform services. Enforces the layer boundary: platform imports from core/kernel, never the reverse.")
PlatformLayer.description: Barrel exports for Layer 2 (Platform). Contains 30+ services: scheduler, task system, agent tools, content system, resources, hosting, projects, governance, QA, economy, and user accounts.

import_boundary.rule: Platform layer (Layer 2) may import from core/ (Layer 1), kernel/ (Layer 0), @pando/shared, @pando/ledger, and npm packages. NEVER upward into api/ or root entry points.

_tags: @gotcha("Detection != sharing. A node may detect claude-code but NOT share it. Own tasks always use full detected capabilities; only shared ones are visible to peers.")
@why("Privacy by default. Operators explicitly opt into sharing compute. Prevents accidental resource exposure.")
LocalCapabilityStore.description: Three-tier capability architecture (Phase 96). Separates detection from sharing: Tier 0 = local private (all detected capabilities, never broadcast), Tier 1 = network shared (explicitly opted in, broadcast via GossipSub), Tier 2 = group scoped (future). Persisted at ~/.pando/local-capabilities.json.

_tags: @gotcha("Rollback is cumulative -- a failure at stage 5 (build) rolls back stage 4 (patch) AND stage 3 (backup). Each stage tracks its own rollback info.")
@why("Sequential pipeline with per-stage rollback ensures the codebase is never left in a broken state, even if the build or QA fails.")
PipelineRunner.description: 7-stage autonomous code pipeline (Phase 16.7): version check -> extract diff -> backup -> apply patch -> build -> QA -> commit. Full rollback at each stage on failure. Wires CodePipeline, QaRunner, DeployManager, VersionProtocol, and Guardrails.

_tags: @gotcha("API keys are hashed with SHA-256 before storage. validateApiKey() hashes the input and scans all active projects for a match. This is O(n) per validation.")
@why("Hashing API keys prevents credential leakage through P2P sync. Any node can validate a key by hash without ever seeing the plaintext.")
ProjectRegistry.description: P2P project metadata registry (Phase 63). Syncs project metadata via GossipSub on pando/projects topic. SQLite + in-memory cache. API keys stored as SHA-256 hashes only -- plaintext never stored or synced. validateApiKey() is critical for Resource Proxy.

_tags: @gotcha("All writes go to MongoDB first (must succeed), then SQLite cache is updated. loadFromBackend() must be called on startup to hydrate SQLite from MongoDB. Without it, queries return stale or empty data.")
@why("MongoDB-first ensures data durability across node restarts. SQLite cache provides fast synchronous reads for the HTTP API layer.")
ProjectStore.description: MongoDB-first project storage (Phase 31.1, 57). Full project lifecycle: CRUD, collaborators, invites, ownership transfers, deployments, ratings, marketplace queries, content reports. SQLite as local cache, MongoDB as source of truth.

_tags: @gotcha("Playwright is imported dynamically at runtime via import('playwright'). If not installed, page tests are skipped gracefully. API tests always work.")
@why("Dynamic import prevents Playwright from being a hard production dependency. Most nodes only need API testing; page testing is optional.")
QaRunner.description: Automated testing runner with Playwright page tests, API endpoint tests, P2P consistency tests, and health checks. 30s per-page timeout, 5-min total timeout. Dynamic Playwright import to avoid hard dependency.

_tags: @gotcha("Built-in tests are only loaded on first run (when persisted file is empty). After that, tests come from the JSON file. Deleting the file resets to builtins.")
@why("Auto-growing suite means every successful deployment adds test coverage. The suite accumulates knowledge about what works.")
RegressionSuite.description: Persistent auto-growing regression test suite. 14 built-in tests (API health, auth gating, governance, ledger, emissions, security). Auto-grows from QA results via addTestFromQAResult(). Persisted at ~/.pando/regression-suite.json. 10-min total timeout, 30s per test.

_tags: @gotcha("MAX_VOTE_WEIGHT is 10.0 -- even the highest-reputation node cannot dominate a vote. MIN_VOTE_WEIGHT is 0.1 so low-rep peers still have some say.")
@why("Sybil resistance through reputation weighting. Creating many low-reputation nodes gives less voting power than one high-reputation node.")
ReputationWeightedGovernance.description: Reputation-weighted governance voting (Phase 12.4). Vote weight = reputation * uptime_factor * resource_factor, clamped [0.1, 10.0]. Prevents Sybil attacks by weighting quality not quantity. Minimum reputation thresholds for proposing (0.3) and voting (0.1).

_tags: @gotcha("Will silently not start if CredentialStore is null -- only trusted compute nodes with CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY run health checks.")
@why("Health checks require decrypted credentials to ping services. Running them only on trusted nodes prevents credential exposure.")
ResourceHealthChecker.description: Periodic health checks on contributed resources (MongoDB ping, S3 HEAD, GitHub API, OpenAI models). Only runs on nodes with CredentialStore access (trusted compute). Results stored in memory, exposed via GET /v1/resources/health.

_tags: @gotcha("Default prices are hardcoded constants. Operators override via setPrice() but there is no persistence -- prices reset on restart.")
@why("Separating marketplace from routing allows independent price negotiation without affecting task execution logic.")
ResourceMarketplace.description: Marketplace pricing for network resources. Operators set per-capability Lux prices, buyers find cheapest providers. Prices broadcast via GossipSub, cached locally for fast lookups.

_tags: @gotcha("Gateway rewards are per 1000 requests and relay rewards are per MB -- unit divisors normalize raw counts before applying reward rates.")
@why("Metering is separated from billing so that usage data can be audited independently of payment logic.")
ResourceMeter.description: Per-capability resource usage metering and Lux reward calculation. Tracks usage records per node, persists to disk, prunes records older than 30 days, calculates rewards based on per-capability rates.

_tags: @gotcha("Scores use exponential decay (0.95 per challenge round) so recent proofs matter more than old ones. Max 500 scores and 50 results per peer.")
@why("Proof challenges prevent nodes from claiming capabilities they do not actually provide. Sybil-resistant because challenges require real computation.")
ResourceProofChallenger.description: Periodic proof-of-resource challenges: storage (SHA-256 hash of random payload), compute (task verification within calibrated time), bandwidth (relay delivery within timeout). Scores decayed by 0.95 factor for recency weighting.

_tags: @gotcha("Credentials are NEVER stored in SQLite or transmitted over P2P. Only SHA-256 hashed metadata is synced. CredentialStore on trusted EC2 nodes handles the actual secrets.")
@why("Two-tier trust model: metadata is public (all nodes), credentials are private (EC2 only). Prevents credential leakage through P2P gossip.")
ResourceRegistry.description: P2P metadata registry for shared resources. Syncs METADATA ONLY via GossipSub (no credentials in P2P). In-memory Map + SQLite persistence. CredentialStore (MongoDB) handles encrypted credential CRUD separately.

resource_registry_public_ip.what: Tier 2 deploys routed to wrong IP because resource discovery used internal addresses
resource_registry_public_ip.why: EC2 nodes behind VPC NAT have no public IP in their profile without explicit configuration
resource_registry_public_ip.fix: publicAddress field must be set via PUBLIC_IP env var on EC2 for correct address discovery

_tags: @gotcha("Failure tracking uses two thresholds: 3 consecutive failures = degraded (lower score), 5 = disabled (excluded from routing).")
@why("Auto-degradation prevents repeated routing to broken nodes without requiring manual intervention.")
ResourceRouter.description: Smart task routing with failure tracking and auto-degradation. Scores nodes by capability match, reputation, and resource health. Forwards tasks to remote nodes via RequestReplyManager. Auto-disables resources after 5 consecutive failures.

_tags: @gotcha("Distribution shares differ by project type: private=85% owner, shared=custom or equal split, public=50% contributors + 30% network treasury. Lux transfers go through the P2P ledger, not MongoDB.")
@why("Revenue distribution stays on the P2P ledger (economy is network state) while revenue records are in MongoDB (user data). This matches the stateless-node architecture.")
RevenueEngine.description: Usage metering, revenue collection, and automatic Lux distribution (Phase 31.4, 57). Records revenue events, manages subscriptions with auto-renewal, charges usage fees, distributes revenue to stakeholders based on project type (private: 85/10/5, public: 50/30/15/5).

revenue_mongodb_first.rule: All revenue records and subscriptions must be written to MongoDB first. SQLite is cache only. If MongoDB write fails, the operation fails.

_tags: @gotcha("Does NOT spawn agents or create workspaces -- that moved to AgentManager in Phase 27. This is a PURE EXECUTOR.")
@why("Separating scheduling from agent lifecycle prevents deadlocks and allows independent scaling of queue management vs compute.")
Scheduler.description: Thin task queue executor. Manages approved-task queue, tracks metrics, emits task events, handles parent/child cascade completion, recovers orphaned tasks, auto-archives old tasks.

scheduler_pure_executor.what: Scheduler deadlocked when it contained agent spawning and decision logic
scheduler_pure_executor.why: Mixing queue management with agent lifecycle created circular dependencies and blocking waits
scheduler_pure_executor.fix: Made Scheduler a pure executor — dequeues and checks capacity only. Agent spawning moved to AgentManager.

_tags: @gotcha("Result, cost, and role metadata are denormalized into the tasks table for query speed rather than normalized into separate tables.")
@why("Follows the same pattern as packages/ledger/src/database.ts: single responsibility for SQL, row-to-object mappers, and prepared statements.")
TaskDatabase.description: SQLite persistence layer for the task queue. WAL mode, prepared statements, denormalized result/cost/role fields for query speed. All SQL lives here -- TaskQueue delegates persistence to this module.

_tags: @gotcha("On first startup migrates from legacy tasks.json if present. Renames old file to tasks.json.migrated.")
@why("SQLite gives ACID guarantees for concurrent task claims that JSON files cannot provide.")
TaskQueue.description: SQLite-backed priority task queue with atomic claims, file conflict detection, dependency tracking, P2P sync via GossipSub, and JSON legacy migration.

_tags: @gotcha("listThreads() is SYNC -- returns cached index. loadFromBackend() must be called first to hydrate from MongoDB. If not called, the store appears empty.")
@why("StorageBackend abstraction allows same code to work with MongoDB (compute nodes) or P2P proxy (user nodes) transparently.")
ThreadStore.description: Persistent threaded conversation storage (Phase 24.9). All CRUD through StorageBackend (MongoDB-first, Phase 57). Supports per-thread encryption keys (Phase 41), user ownership (Phase 31), and project linking. Max 200 threads cached in memory.

_tags: @gotcha("Sessions removed in Phase 86 -- auth is now stateless JWT issued by api-server. Guest private keys are encrypted with node-level secret; claimed accounts re-encrypt with user password. Browser-key guests store NO private key on node (enc_type='browser').")
@why("P2P-synced auth means any node can verify credentials without a central auth server. Private keys stay local (never synced) for security.")
UserAccountStore.description: P2P-synced user accounts (Phase 56, 86). Auth data (username, password_hash) lives in ledger accounts table via GossipSub. Local-only data (encrypted private keys) in auth-local.db. Guests auto-created with Ed25519 keypairs, claimable with username+password. Stateless JWT auth (Phase 86).

private_keys_local_only.rule: Private keys are NEVER transmitted over P2P or stored in the synced ledger. They exist only in auth-local.db on the node where the guest was created.

_tags: @gotcha("Must be the FIRST import in cli.ts/tui.ts — if anything imports libp2p before this, it crashes on Node 18/20.")
Polyfills.description: Promise.withResolvers polyfill for Node.js < 22. Required by libp2p's it-queue dependency. Must be imported before any other modules.

_tags: @gotcha("CONTEXT_MAP must be updated when gateway pages or node files are renamed — stale paths cause missed context detection.")
@why("Pre-screening before LLM saves API calls and provides instant cost estimates to users.")
SmartRouter.description: Phase 18.4/18.5 heuristic classifier. Detects context files from user messages via keyword-to-file mapping, estimates task complexity (trivial→project), attaches Lux cost/time estimates. Pure heuristics, no LLM, deterministic, zero-cost. Sits between user input and task creation.

_tags: @gotcha("Auto-creates identity on first run with NO prompts. Only prompts for password if existing identity is encrypted.")
@gotcha("Use 127.0.0.1 in gateway URL, never 'localhost' — IPv6 resolution causes failures on some systems.")
@gotcha("Custom readline history management (historySize: 0) because the TUI implements its own history with arrow key navigation.")
@why("TUI intercepts console.log/console.error to insert output ABOVE the prompt line without disrupting user input — uses raw terminal escape sequences.")
TuiEntryPoint.description: Interactive terminal with readline, ANSI coloring, slash commands, autocomplete, spinner animations, and identity management (create/encrypt/decrypt/switch).

_tags: @gotcha("privateKey in NodeIdentity is protobuf-wrapped (68 bytes: 4 header + 32 seed + 32 pub). Raw 32-byte seed must be extracted for X25519 conversion (subarray 4..36).")
@gotcha("loadOrCreateIdentity throws if identity.json is encrypted — use TUI or --data-dir to handle encrypted identities.")
@gotcha("Multiple identities stored in ~/.pando/identities/<peerId>.json. Legacy single identity in ~/.pando/identity.json still supported.")
@why("Session file (~/.pando/session.json) caches the decrypted identity so users don't re-enter password on every restart. Deleted on /logout.")
@why("verifySignature manually builds protobuf-wrapped public key bytes (0x08 0x01 0x12 0x20 + 32-byte key) because publicKeyFromProtobuf expects this format.")
SharedCrypto.description: Ed25519 identity management (generate, save, load, encrypt, decrypt), session management, message signing/verification, transaction signing, and multi-identity support.

PUBKEY_EXTRACTION.what: Cross-node JWT verification failed because public key was looked up in ledger
PUBKEY_EXTRACTION.why: Ledger stored 'remote-peer' as public key for nodes registered via P2P sync
PUBKEY_EXTRACTION.fix: Extract public key directly from peerId string via peerIdFromString().publicKey — Ed25519 peerIds embed the full 32-byte public key

SharedIndex.description: Barrel re-export of all shared types and crypto functions consumed by every other Pando package.

_tags: @gotcha("MESSAGE_VERSION = 1 — must be incremented when envelope format changes, or P2P messages will be silently dropped by peers on different versions.")
@gotcha("OperationalMode 1/2/3 maps to local-only / P2P / full (P2P + internet infra). Mode 1 must always be available offline.")
@gotcha("LUX_HARD_CAP = 10,000,000,000 — this constant is the single source of truth for the Lux supply ceiling, checked in TransactionStore.emit().")
@gotcha("MessageType.PEER_EXCHANGE is handled in PandoNode (index.ts), not PandoNetwork — it's an application-level protocol, not a kernel primitive.")
@why("NodeHealth tracks per-layer boot status (kernel/core/platform) so the node can degrade gracefully instead of crashing entirely.")
SharedTypes.description: All shared types, interfaces, enums, and constants used across every Pando package — identity, messages, transactions, governance, agents, capabilities, and economics.

HARD_CAP_IMMUTABLE.rule: LUX_HARD_CAP (10 billion) must never be changed without Tier 1 governance vote (90% quorum + 30-day migration)

  const res = await fetch(`${PANDO_NODE_URL}/v1/wallet`, { headers: authHeaders(), signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) });

  const text = [
    `Pando Wallet`,
    `  Peer ID (address): ${data.peerId}`,
    `  Public Key:        ${data.publicKey}`,
    `  Balance:           ${data.balance} Lux`,
    `  Identity Created:  ${new Date(data.createdAt).toISOString()}`,
    `  Data Directory:    ${data.dataDir}`,
    `  Identity File:     ${data.ownership?.identityFile}`,

    `Backup:    ${data.ownership?.backup}`,

private generateMonitorScript(): string {
    return `#!/bin/bash
# Pando Instance Security Monitor — Phase 64
# Runs as root. Detects unauthorized access. Wipes and shuts down on intrusion.

echo "[pando-monitor] Security monitor started at $(date -u)"

# Wait for bootstrap to fully complete before arming tripwire
# (cloud-init runs bash as root, which would trigger false positives)
echo "[pando-monitor] Waiting for cloud-init to finish..."
cloud-init status --wait 2>/dev/null || sleep 60
echo "[pando-monitor] Armed at $(date -u)"

PANDO_PID=""

    const safeSummary = sanitizeText(summary);
    const record: ActivityRecord = {
      id: createHash('sha256').update(`${this.localPeerId}:${Date.now()}:${action}:${safeSummary}`).digest('hex'),
      agentId: this.localPeerId,
      nodeId: this.localPeerId,
      agentRole: 'node',
      agentTier: 1,
      modelId: 'pando-node',
      action,
      timestamp: Date.now(),
      summary: safeSummary,
      proposalId,
      signature: 'pending',

private insertRecord(record: ContentRecord): void {
    this.db.prepare(`
      INSERT OR REPLACE INTO content_records (
        content_id, type, title, description, owner_peer_id, builder_peer_id,
        repo_url, live_url, hosting_nodes, version, version_hash, status,
        tags, lux_earned, manifest, created_at, updated_at
      ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
    `).run(
      record.contentId, record.type, record.title, record.description,
      record.ownerPeerId, record.builderPeerId || null,
      record.repoUrl || null, record.liveUrl || null,
      JSON.stringify(record.hostingNodes), record.version,
      record.versionHash, record.status, JSON.stringify(record.tags),
      record.luxEarned, JSON.stringify(record.manifest),

private rowToReport(row: any): ContentReport {
    return {
      id: row.id,
      projectId: row.project_id,
      reporterId: row.reporter_id,
      reason: row.reason as ReportReason,
      description: row.description || '',
      status: row.status as ReportStatus,
      aiReview: row.ai_review || '',
      aiSafetyScore: row.ai_safety_score ?? -1,
      reviewedBy: row.reviewed_by || '',
      resolvedAt: row.resolved_at || 0,
      createdAt: row.created_at,
    };

getDefaultApiTests(): ApiTestCase[] {
    return [
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/status', expectedStatus: 200, expectedFields: ['peerId', 'uptime', 'peers'], description: 'Node status endpoint' },
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/health', expectedStatus: 200, expectedFields: ['status'], description: 'Health check endpoint' },
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/peers', expectedStatus: 200, expectedFields: ['peers'], description: 'Peer list endpoint' },
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/tasks', expectedStatus: 200, description: 'Task list endpoint' },
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/governance/proposals', expectedStatus: 200, description: 'Governance proposals' },
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/monitor/status', expectedStatus: 200, description: 'Monitor status' },
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/wallet', expectedStatus: 200, expectedFields: ['peerId', 'balance'], description: 'Wallet info' },
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/emissions/stats', expectedStatus: 200, description: 'Emission statistics' },
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/security/stats', expectedStatus: 200, description: 'Security statistics' },
      // Auth-required endpoints — should return 401 without token
      { method: 'POST', path: '/v1/tasks', expectedStatus: 401, authRequired: false, description: 'Task creation requires auth' },
      { method: 'POST', path: '/v1/transfer', expectedStatus: 401, authRequired: false, description: 'Transfer requires auth' },
      { method: 'POST', path: '/v1/upgrade', expectedStatus: 401, authRequired: false, description: 'Upgrade requires auth' },

      success: false,
      totalPages: pageCount,
      passed: 0,
      failed: 0,
      errors: pageCount,
      timeouts: 0,
      pages: Array.from({ length: pageCount }, (_, i) => ({
        url: `page-${i}`,
        status: 'error' as const,
        consoleErrors: [],
        durationMs: 0,
        error: 'Playwright is not installed. Install with: npm install playwright',
      })),

ResourceRegistry.persistRecord.source_lines:
private persistRecord(record: ResourceRecord): void {
    this.stmtInsert.run(
      record.resourceId,
      record.type,
      record.userId || null,
      JSON.stringify(record.grantedTo),
      record.maxUsagePerDay,
      record.pricePerUnit,
      record.registeredAt,
      record.expiresAt,
      record.status,
      record.metadata ? JSON.stringify(record.metadata) : null,
    );
  }

MonitorConfig.source_lines:
export interface MonitorConfig {
  checkIntervalMs: number;        // How often to check health (default: 30s)
  stuckPeerThresholdMs: number;   // Alert if 0 peers for this long (default: 5min)
  failureRateThreshold: number;   // Alert if failure rate exceeds this (default: 0.5 = 50%)
  failureRateWindowMs: number;    // Window for failure rate calculation (default: 1h)
  maxConsecutiveFailures: number;  // Alert after N consecutive task failures (default: 3)
  memoryUsageThreshold: number;   // Alert if heap used exceeds this fraction (default: 0.85 = 85%)
  eventLoopLagThresholdMs: number; // Alert if event loop lag exceeds this (default: 500ms)
  ledgerSyncLagThresholdMs: number; // Alert if ledger sync stale longer than this (default: 10min)
  spawnFailureRateThreshold: number; // Alert if agent spawn failure rate exceeds this (default: 0.6 = 60%)
  spawnFailureWindowMs: number;   // Window for spawn failure rate calculation (default: 30min)
}

export type MonitorHealthStatus = 'healthy' | 'degraded' | 'critical';
export type MonitorAlertSeverity = 'info' | 'warning' | 'critical';

  type: string;              // Request type: "profile_query", "verify_code", "health_check", etc.
  payload: any;              // Request data (must fit in 8KB with envelope)
  timeout: number;           // ms — how long sender waits for reply
  timestamp: number;
}

export interface PandoReply {
  requestId: string;         // Matches the request
  from: string;              // Responder peer ID
  to: string;                // Original requester peer ID
  type: string;              // Same type as request

PandoLedger.recordActivity.source_lines:
recordActivity(record: ActivityRecord): void {
    const stmt = this.db.prepare(`
      INSERT OR IGNORE INTO activity
        (id, agent_id, node_id, agent_role, agent_tier, model_id, action, timestamp, summary, details, proposal_id, task_id, transaction_id, signature, received_at)
      VALUES
        (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
    `);
    stmt.run(
      record.id,
      record.agentId,
      record.nodeId,
      record.agentRole,
      record.agentTier,

async function handleWallet() {
  const res = await fetch(`${PANDO_NODE_URL}/v1/wallet`, { headers: authHeaders(), signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) });
  const data = await res.json() as any;

  const text = [
    `Pando Wallet`,
    `  Peer ID (address): ${data.peerId}`,
    `  Public Key:        ${data.publicKey}`,
    `  Balance:           ${data.balance} Lux`,
    `  Identity Created:  ${new Date(data.createdAt).toISOString()}`,
    `  Data Directory:    ${data.dataDir}`,
    `  Identity File:     ${data.ownership?.identityFile}`,
    ``,
    `Ownership: ${data.ownership?.explanation}`,
    `Backup:    ${data.ownership?.backup}`,

private generateMonitorScript(): string {
    return `#!/bin/bash
# Pando Instance Security Monitor — Phase 64
# Runs as root. Detects unauthorized access. Wipes and shuts down on intrusion.

echo "[pando-monitor] Security monitor started at $(date -u)"

# Wait for bootstrap to fully complete before arming tripwire
# (cloud-init runs bash as root, which would trigger false positives)
echo "[pando-monitor] Waiting for cloud-init to finish..."
cloud-init status --wait 2>/dev/null || sleep 60
echo "[pando-monitor] Armed at $(date -u)"

PANDO_PID=""

      agentId: this.localPeerId,
      nodeId: this.localPeerId,
      agentRole: 'node',
      agentTier: 1,
      modelId: 'pando-node',
      action,

      summary: safeSummary,
      proposalId,

private insertRecord(record: ContentRecord): void {
    this.db.prepare(`
      INSERT OR REPLACE INTO content_records (
        content_id, type, title, description, owner_peer_id, builder_peer_id,
        repo_url, live_url, hosting_nodes, version, version_hash, status,
        tags, lux_earned, manifest, created_at, updated_at
      ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
    `).run(
      record.contentId, record.type, record.title, record.description,
      record.ownerPeerId, record.builderPeerId || null,
      record.repoUrl || null, record.liveUrl || null,
      JSON.stringify(record.hostingNodes), record.version,
      record.versionHash, record.status, JSON.stringify(record.tags),
      record.luxEarned, JSON.stringify(record.manifest),

      liveUrl: row.live_url || undefined,

private rowToReport(row: any): ContentReport {
    return {
      id: row.id,
      projectId: row.project_id,
      reporterId: row.reporter_id,
      reason: row.reason as ReportReason,
      description: row.description || '',
      status: row.status as ReportStatus,
      aiReview: row.ai_review || '',
      aiSafetyScore: row.ai_safety_score ?? -1,
      reviewedBy: row.reviewed_by || '',
      resolvedAt: row.resolved_at || 0,
      createdAt: row.created_at,
    };

getDefaultApiTests(): ApiTestCase[] {
    return [
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/status', expectedStatus: 200, expectedFields: ['peerId', 'uptime', 'peers'], description: 'Node status endpoint' },
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/health', expectedStatus: 200, expectedFields: ['status'], description: 'Health check endpoint' },
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/peers', expectedStatus: 200, expectedFields: ['peers'], description: 'Peer list endpoint' },
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/tasks', expectedStatus: 200, description: 'Task list endpoint' },
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/governance/proposals', expectedStatus: 200, description: 'Governance proposals' },
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/monitor/status', expectedStatus: 200, description: 'Monitor status' },
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/wallet', expectedStatus: 200, expectedFields: ['peerId', 'balance'], description: 'Wallet info' },
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/emissions/stats', expectedStatus: 200, description: 'Emission statistics' },
      { method: 'GET', path: '/v1/security/stats', expectedStatus: 200, description: 'Security statistics' },
      // Auth-required endpoints — should return 401 without token
      { method: 'POST', path: '/v1/tasks', expectedStatus: 401, authRequired: false, description: 'Task creation requires auth' },
      { method: 'POST', path: '/v1/transfer', expectedStatus: 401, authRequired: false, description: 'Transfer requires auth' },
      { method: 'POST', path: '/v1/upgrade', expectedStatus: 401, authRequired: false, description: 'Upgrade requires auth' },

private playwrightUnavailableResult(startedAt: number, pageCount: number): QAResult {
    return {
      success: false,
      totalPages: pageCount,
      passed: 0,
      failed: 0,
      errors: pageCount,
      timeouts: 0,
      pages: Array.from({ length: pageCount }, (_, i) => ({
        url: `page-${i}`,
        status: 'error' as const,
        consoleErrors: [],
        durationMs: 0,
        error: 'Playwright is not installed. Install with: npm install playwright',
      })),

private persistRecord(record: ResourceRecord): void {
    this.stmtInsert.run(
      record.resourceId,
      record.type,
      record.userId || null,
      JSON.stringify(record.grantedTo),
      record.maxUsagePerDay,
      record.pricePerUnit,
      record.registeredAt,
      record.expiresAt,
      record.status,
      record.metadata ? JSON.stringify(record.metadata) : null,
    );
  }

TaskDatabase.rowToTask.source_lines:
private rowToTask(row: any): Task {
    const task: Task = {
      id: row.id,
      title: row.title,
      description: row.description || '',
      status: row.status as TaskStatus,
      priority: row.priority as TaskPriority,
      createdBy: row.created_by || '',
      assignedTo: row.assigned_to || null,
      createdAt: row.created_at,
      updatedAt: row.updated_at,
      files: this.getFiles(row.id),
      dependencies: this.getDependencies(row.id),
    };

MonitorConfig.name: MonitorConfig
MonitorConfig.source_lines:
export interface MonitorConfig {
  checkIntervalMs: number;        // How often to check health (default: 30s)
  stuckPeerThresholdMs: number;   // Alert if 0 peers for this long (default: 5min)
  failureRateThreshold: number;   // Alert if failure rate exceeds this (default: 0.5 = 50%)
  failureRateWindowMs: number;    // Window for failure rate calculation (default: 1h)
  maxConsecutiveFailures: number;  // Alert after N consecutive task failures (default: 3)
  memoryUsageThreshold: number;   // Alert if heap used exceeds this fraction (default: 0.85 = 85%)
  eventLoopLagThresholdMs: number; // Alert if event loop lag exceeds this (default: 500ms)
  ledgerSyncLagThresholdMs: number; // Alert if ledger sync stale longer than this (default: 10min)
  spawnFailureRateThreshold: number; // Alert if agent spawn failure rate exceeds this (default: 0.6 = 60%)
  spawnFailureWindowMs: number;   // Window for spawn failure rate calculation (default: 30min)
}

export type MonitorHealthStatus = 'healthy' | 'degraded' | 'critical';
export type MonitorAlertSeverity = 'info' | 'warning' | 'critical';

PandoRequest.name: PandoRequest
PandoRequest.source_lines:
export interface PandoRequest {
  requestId: string;         // UUID
  from: string;              // Sender peer ID
  to: string;                // Target peer ID (or "*" for broadcast query)
  type: string;              // Request type: "profile_query", "verify_code", "health_check", etc.
  payload: any;              // Request data (must fit in 8KB with envelope)
  timeout: number;           // ms — how long sender waits for reply
  timestamp: number;
}

export interface PandoReply {
  requestId: string;         // Matches the request
  from: string;              // Responder peer ID

export interface AgentTemplate {
  role: string;               // 'manager', 'builder', 'tester', 'reviewer', 'researcher', 'devops'
  template: string;           // Markdown instructions for the agent
  version: number;            // Template version — for marketplace update checks
  capabilities: AgentCapabilityDeclaration;
  publisherPeerId?: string;   // Who published this (set for marketplace agents)
  requiredBackends?: string[]; // Specific AI backends needed (e.g. ['ollama'])
}

export interface AgentCapabilityDeclaration {
  textAI: boolean;         // Needs text generation (LLM)
  imageAI: boolean;        // Needs image generation (ComfyUI, DALL-E)
  codeExecution: boolean;  // Needs Claude Code-style execution (file edits, bash)
  localFiles: boolean;     // Needs Local Environment file access (v2.5)
  internet: boolean;       // Needs outbound HTTP (fetch to external URLs)
